title: U.S. ambassador calls ongoing West Bank settler violence an "act of terror"
summary: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee met with about 10 Palestinian American residents who described the impact of the violence on their lives and properties.
story: The U.S. ambassador to Israel condemned Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank again on Saturday, calling the behavior an "act of terror" as he visited with Palestinian American residents shaken by months of attacks.

"If there are squatters that come in and put up their own flags and take possession of something that does not belong to them, if they burn a car, if they torch a mosque, if they go into someone's home and vandalize it, paint graffiti on the walls, that's a criminal act. But it extends beyond a criminal act. It's an act of terror," Ambassador Mike Huckabee said during his visit to the village of Turmus Ayya, which has reported frequent attacks by settlers over the past year.
Such attacks have surged since the war in Gaza began with the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, according to the United Nations humanitarian office.

During Saturday's visit to Turmus Ayya, the ambassador began his remarks by making clear he was addressing U.S. citizens, who make up a small percentage of the roughly 3 million Palestinians in the West Bank.

"I'm very aware that a lot of the American people who live in Turmus Ayya and other communities across this region are not enjoying the life they deserve to live, not enjoying it in a peaceful way," Huckabee said. "It's a life that is disturbed by people who have created extraordinary challenges that are unfair and illegal."

The U.S. Embassy can't investigate criminal activity, he said, but it can tell its host government "there are needs that need to be addressed, there are issues that cannot go unnoticed, and specific crimes and acts of terror that cannot continue without that country doing the investigation and adjudication that every person has a right to expect."
Huckabee met with about 10 Palestinian American residents who described the impact of the violence on their lives and properties, the municipality told The Associated Press.
A week ago, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the actions of a "handful of rioters," and the foreign ministry called the settlers' actions "a disgrace."
Netanyahu's government is the most ultranationalist and religious in Israel's history. It has presided over a surge of settlement construction in the West Bank.

Israel captured the West Bank, along with Gaza and East Jerusalem, in the 1967 Mideast war, territories the Palestinians want for a future state. The U.N. and much of the international community consider them to be illegally occupied.
Since then, the Israeli government has built nearly 150 settlements that are home to well over 500,000 Jewish settlers. Many settlements resemble developed suburbs.

Israel's military operates in all parts of the West Bank, but rights groups have said the military frequently turns a blind eye to settler violence. The settlers are Israeli citizens, and Israel's defense minister recently announced plans to fully transfer law enforcement among settlers to the Israeli police.

title: Colombia drone attack by suspected guerrillas kills 3 soldiers, army says
summary: Recently elected President Abelardo de la Espriella​ condemned the attack.
story: An attack involving explosives dropped from drones followed by a clash inside a military compound in northeastern Colombia has killed at least three soldiers and wounded four, Colombia's army said Saturday.

Local authorities blamed the attack late Friday on the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN). It targeted a military unit in the municipality of Ocaña, in the Norte de Santander department, which borders Venezuela. Two soldiers died at the site and a third after receiving medical attention, Colombia's military said on X.

"In the context of the operations deployed following these events, Captain Marco David Pirajón Montezuma, Professional Soldier Joel Alberto Jiménez Jaramillo, and Professional Soldier Jhon Carlos Marrugo Manjarrez were killed during an engagement in combat, while honorably and committedly carrying out their duty in service to the Nation," the military said.
President Abelardo de la Espriella condemned the attack.
"For every police officer or soldier murdered, we will bring the full weight and legitimate force of the State down upon the criminals," the president said.

De la Espriella, a millionaire who earned President Trump's endorsement, won a close runoff election in June. He started his four-year term on Aug. 7. Since taking office, De la Espriella has joined the Shield of the Americas, an anti-cartel alliance headed by the U.S.
He has said he plans to forge a military alliance with Israel and the U.S. to help strengthen his war against Colombia's guerrillas.

Much of ELN, an armed group active since 1964, is based in the Catatumbo region, which includes parts of the Norte de Santander and Cesar departments. ELN also harbors dissident factions of the now-defunct Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) that did not join the peace agreement a decade ago.
Both groups are vying for control of the strategic region, which connects to the porous border with Venezuela and is one of Colombia's primary coca-producing areas.

In August, an explosion outside a police station in Cucuta injured 11 police officers and killed a police dog. Officials also blamed that attack on the ELN. Earlier this week, at least one civilian was killed and 11 other people were injured after a car bomb exploded outside a police station in northeastern Colombia.

title: Painting looted by Nazis to be returned to collector's heir
summary: The painting was among the artworks looted and sold under duress to Nazi officials from art dealer Jacques Goudstikker after Adolf Hitler's Germany invaded the Netherlands in 1940.
story: A 17th-century Italian painting looted by Nazis from a prominent Jewish Dutch art collector must be returned to the rightful owner's heir, a judge in Argentina ruled on Friday.

Judge Santiago Inchausti approved a deal in which the daughter of a fugitive Nazi official agreed to give up her claim to the painting rather than face trial. This paves the way for the long-sought return of "Portrait of a Lady" to Maril von Saher, the sole surviving heir of art dealer Jacques Goudstikker. His much-celebrated collection of 1,100 paintings was sold under duress to Nazi officials after Adolf Hitler's Germany invaded the Netherlands in 1940.
The painting was recognized by the Dutch newspaper Algemeen Dagblad in a photo of a house for sale in the Argentine seaside resort of Mar del Plata in August 2025.

The painting was hanging above a green sofa in the living room of Patricia Kadgien, whose father, Friedrich Kadgien, was a financier for the Nazi SS paramilitary organization. He was one of the several high-ranking Nazis to escape to the South American country after World War II.

Patricia Kadgien and her husband, Juan Carlos Cortegoso, were charged with aggravated cover-up last year after authorities said they hid the 18th-century painting despite knowing Argentine and international investigators were seeking it.

Under the agreement, a copy obtained by The Associated Press, the couple agreed to give up any claim to the work and consent to its return to von Saher in exchange for avoiding a criminal trial and spending two years under court supervision. During that time, they must make payments to a hospital in Argentina's coastal city of Mar del Plata, where they live, and keep authorities informed of their whereabouts.

For decades, the portrait had been identified as a work by the Italian Baroque painter Giuseppe Vittore Ghislandi. It appeared under that attribution in Goudstikker's collection records and was exhibited as a Ghislandi in Amsterdam before the war. But a court-ordered examination by Argentina's National Academy of Fine Arts reached a different conclusion, attributing the work to the Italian artist Giacomo Antonio Melchiorre Ceruti.
Experts authenticated the painting as part of Goudstikker's collection and estimated its value at about $290,000.

Goudstikker was one of Europe's leading art dealers before World War II, known for a collection that included works by Rembrandt and Vermeer. He died in a shipwreck while fleeing Amsterdam with his family as German forces swept into the Netherlands in May 1940.

An estimated 1,100 works from his collection were illegally sold to Hermann Göring, known as Hitler's right-hand man, who amassed a vast art collection during the war. It remains unclear exactly how "Portrait of a Lady" came into the possession of Kadgien, Göring's financial adviser, who handled foreign currency, precious metals and the sale of confiscated property for the Nazi regime.
Kadgien fled Europe after Germany's defeat, first to Switzerland and later to Argentina. He died in the South American country in 1978 without having been arrested or charged with war crimes.

Lawyers for von Saher, who now lives in Greenwich, Connecticut, and spent decades trying to recover her family's looted art, said she has agreed to let the painting be exhibited in Argentina before being returned to her.

During last year's raids on homes owned by Kadgien and her sister in Mar del Plata, Argentine police also seized two 19th-century paintings, along with other prints and engravings. Authorities are still investigating whether any of them may also have been looted during World War II.

title: Senior aides to U.K.'s Nigel Farage step down in scandal over undercover report
summary: Two senior aides to Nigel Farage, the firebrand leader of the U.K.'s populist Reform party, have stepped down in the wake of an investigative news report.
story: Two senior aides to Nigel Farage, the firebrand leader of the U.K.'s populist Reform party, have stepped down after the party was accused of breaking British electoral law concerning foreign funding in the wake of an investigative news report where a journalist posed as a wealthy American's son who wanted to donate to the party.

In a statement, a spokesperson for the party said it was launching an internal probe after the report aired on Britain's Channel 4 news late Thursday. Two Reform party officials, James Orr and Dan Jukes, have left their positions pending the outcome of that investigation, the spokesperson said.

"The party believes it is important that the investigation is allowed to proceed independently and without prejudice. No further comment will be made while the investigation is ongoing," the spokesperson said.

Jukes is widely regarded as Farage's right-hand man, with an "innate sense of his boss' instinct," according to CBS News' partner network BBC News. Orr, an influential figure in the British national conservative movement, served as Reform's head of policy until his resignation. He is a theologian and associate professor of the philosophy of religion at the University of Cambridge. Both men denied any wrongdoing.
In an interview with a London radio station early Friday, Farage insisted the party had broken no laws.

"The party has not taken any dodgy money or anything like that whatsoever," Farage told LBC Radio. "However, it is a clear case of entrapment, and they worked at it for a very long time, and they got a couple of our contractors to say things that perhaps should not have been said. And as a result of that, they have been removed this morning and yeah, you know, I'm not happy about it."
Channel 4 stood by the report, with a spokesperson telling BBC News the investigation "has been rigorously verified to ensure accuracy. We would encourage people to watch the investigation in full."

The allegations pile further pressure on Farage just as his party's annual conference was getting underway. It also unfolds against the backdrop of scrutiny over donations linked to the party, including an ongoing parliamentary investigation over a multimillion-pound donation from cryptobillionaire Christopher Harborne in 2024. Farage denies any wrongdoing.
Speaking to CBS News at the party's conference, Zia Yusuf, a spokesperson for domestic affairs, downplayed any immediate blowback the allegations would have on the party's internal operations.

"Look, Reform has had many great people who have helped get us to where we are. And I have no doubt, given the talent pipeline that I do have visibility of, both at parliamentary level, potentially, and beyond it, we will withstand this, and ultimately, ultimately will come out strong on the other side," Yusuf said.

On Thursday night, Channel 4 aired the investigation that it said was carried out by an undercover team of journalists from a group called Verbatim, which was founded by journalists from the Centre for Climate Reporting.

The investigation follows one journalist who poses as the British-educated son of a wealthy American businessman from Wyoming, who both appeared eager to support the party, which shares aspects of ideology and policy positions with elements of the MAGA movement, as well as other right-leaning populist movements around the world.

British law regards a permissible donor to a U.K. political party as either a U.K.-registered voter or a company. In the scenario that unfolds in the undercover investigation, the son is a permissible donor, and the father is not.

Secretly filmed footage purports to show the two party aides arranging donations from the undercover journalist to fund the commissioning of a number of political polls. According to Channel 4, the donations added up to 32,500 British pounds, which is about $44,000.

Some of those polls later appeared in news articles for British newspapers such as The Telegraph and the Times of London. The articles, which reflect favorably on the party on issues such as its fortunes in local elections and support among labor union members, do not mention how Reform allegedly commissioned the polls.
Jukes is heard telling the undercover journalist that the donation made a "huge impact" for the party while not "showing up anywhere in public records."

Orr denied Reform's involvement in the polling, saying in a video posted to social media an "independent person had paid an independent pollster." "No money reached Reform UK at all, no donation reached Reform UK at all — whether it was in cash or in kind," he said.

The investigation also includes a discussion between Jukes and the journalist on how to circumvent electoral law to secure a separate foreign donation to the party of 500,000 British pounds, or about $675,000. Channel 4 says that donation was never made.
The investigation culminates in a four-way lunch between the journalist posing as the son of the American businessman, an actor playing the businessman, Jukes and Farage.

During that meeting, Farage appears to have knowledge that the funding for the polls came from the businessman, and does not appear to be concerned when the son proposes the method by which the 500,000-pound foreign donation could reach the party, saying, "Thank you. Well, both of you. Thank you."
Jukes released a statement to BBC News calling the report "entrapment over a prolonged period of nearly a year by foreign-funded climate change activists."
"I totally deny any wrongdoing but have stepped back from politics in order to clear my name," Jukes said.

In a statement to Sky News, Orr said, "I have agreed to step down from my current role at Reform UK pending the outcome of the party's internal investigation into the conduct of the program, with which I will cooperate fully."
At least two of Reform's opponents, the ruling Labour Party and the centrist Liberal Democrats, have written to the Metropolitan Police, alleging breaches of electoral law.
In a statement to CBS News, the police said it was aware of reporting "involving political party donations" and alleged breaches of British law relating to polling.
The police have not launched an investigation so far, saying it would "assess the matter and any information provided to us."
The U.K.'s Electoral Commission, which regulates party and election finance, confirmed it was in contact with the police.

"The law requires political parties to report all permissible donations they accept with a value over £11,180 and all impermissible donations over £500," the commission said. "Information about any potential attempt to evade the controls on donations is for the police to consider."

title: Andrew Tate indicted on trafficking, money laundering charges by Romanian prosecutors
summary: Romanian prosecutors have indicted social media influencer Andrew Tate on charges including trafficking minors and money laundering.
story: Romanian prosecutors on Friday indicted social media influencer Andrew Tate on charges of trafficking minors, sex with a minor, and money laundering.

Tate, 39, and his brother Tristan Tate, 38, were first arrested in Romania's capital, Bucharest, in late 2022. Tristan is indicted with complicity in the case, according to DIICOT, Romania's anti-organized crime agency.
The agency said on Friday that the Tate brothers coerced a victim by pretending to be in a loving relationship and then forcing her to produce pornographic material for an online webcam business.
A lawyer for the Tate brothers in Romania did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The new indictment stems from an investigation that led to the brothers' arrest in 2022 and their being formally indicted in 2023. A court returned that case to DIICOT in 2024 because of multiple legal and procedural irregularities on the part of the prosecutors. The case wasn't closed, and there was also a separate legal case against the brothers in Romania in 2024.
The Tates, who are dual U.S.-British citizens, are among the world's most polarizing internet personalities by promoting wealth, male dominance and misogyny through their social media empire.

DIICOT alleges that in 2012 the brothers recruited a 15-year-old girl in Luton, a town in England where the brothers are from, and that they obtained more than $1.2 million from her webcam activity after she was repeatedly transported to Romania.

The crime agency alleges that Tristan Tate knew the victim's age, that she had been recruited by Andrew, and that between 2014 and 2021 he knowingly deceived her about his brother's "feelings and intentions," which helped to facilitate her sexual exploitation. It is further alleged that between December 2020 and mid-2021, Andrew Tate "repeatedly had sexual intercourse and sexual acts with another minor victim," who was also age 15.

Between December 2023 and July 2024, DIICOT alleges the Tates tried to "hide or disguise the illicit origin of the money" obtained from human trafficking by purchasing four luxury cars worth about 825,000 euros ($957,000), and said they had requested the vehicles be confiscated.
Tate brothers repeatedly denied allegations against them
Both the Tate brothers have repeatedly denied the allegations against them. Andrew Tate has also claimed that there is a political conspiracy to silence them.

The Tates were arrested in Bucharest in late 2022 on charges they participated in a criminal ring that lured women to Romania, where they were sexually exploited. Andrew Tate was also charged with rape.
DIICOT alleges in the new indictment that their victims had been paid or intimidated in attempts to influence them "not to give statements or to give false statements."

The Tates are currently being held in Miami after prosecutors in the United Kingdom requested their extradition in July on sex crimes allegations. The Tates took the witness stand in federal court last week and said they can't adequately defend themselves from criminal sex charges if they have to remain in a Miami jail while fighting extradition to the U.K.
Their lawyers repeated arguments from court filings that the U.K.'s extradition request was out of line because their criminal case in Romania is going first.
Romanian officials allowed the Tates to remain free with some restrictions — including reporting to a Bucharest police station — while the proceedings are ongoing.

title: 2 Nepal workers rescued from tunnel 9 days after floods; more voices heard
summary: Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel as emergency teams continued efforts to reach others believed to be trapped and still alive inside, officials said.
story: Kathmandu, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal pulled two hydropower workers from a tunnel Friday as emergency teams raced to find more survivors, spurred on by the dramatic rescues more than a week after the devastating flash floods that killed more than 1,200 people.

CBS News' Ramy Inocencio said there was hope more survivors could emerge from the tunnel — possibly dozens more — as rescuers heard voices coming from deep inside the structure that the was covered by mud and filled with flood water during last week's catastrophe.
The two men were rescued from the Trishuli 3A tunnel nine days after floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, devastated towns and swept away villages in Nepal.
Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane posted about the second rescue on his Facebook page shortly after army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker's rescue.

Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Inocencio in a text message that he was "thrilled" about the two rescues and "hoping to see more survivors." He said it was unclear how many survivors might still be inside the tunnel, but with voices heard, he said the clock was ticking to find and rescue everyone still alive.
Rescuers first heard voices from inside the tunnel Friday morning, enabling them to locate the two men, Neupane said.

Local television news channels showed images of the first rescued worker, covered in mud, being carried from the site on a rescuer's shoulder. Officials said both men were in stable condition and were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.
Mechanical foreman Sanjay Shah said "thank you" when he was pulled out, but he was then advised not to speak due to his weakened condition, Inocencio reported.

Amir Maharjan, brother of the other rescued worker, mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan, told The Associated Press he "can't explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to God." He said the family were on their way to the hospital to see him.
"We couldn't properly eat or drink for 10 days," Kabir Maharjan's wife, Hirashova, told CBS News partner network BBC News. "We were very scared. Now we are all happy. We are even crying."

At least 557 workers from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project along the Trishuli River remain missing, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the main tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

A Nepali energy adviser told Inocencio it was not just a tunnel that goes into the ground next to the Trishuli River, but a system of rooms and chambers that snake up and down, where the workers are apparently stuck.

The adviser also told Inocencio the trapped workers were some of the smartest engineers in Nepal, and they probably have been trying to figure their own way out, and how to get oxygen so they don't run out of air — the biggest risk.

At least 1,287 people were killed in the floods and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country's disaster management agency. China, as of late Wednesday, said 21 people were killed and 541 were missing on the Tibet side of the border.
About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.
Prabesh Subedi contributed to this report.

title: Ig Nobel prizes go to scientists studying cockroach milk, nose-blowing, more
summary: Ten research teams were honored at a satirical science awards ceremony that was hosted outside the U.S. for the first time due to travel concerns. A study of cockroach milk was among the winners.
story: Ten research teams were honored Thursday at a satirical science awards ceremony that was hosted outside the U.S. for the first time due to travel concerns.
Researchers who studied milk from cockroaches and analyzed soil health using underwear received Ig Nobel prizes celebrating unusual and imaginative contributions to science.
The awards, organized by a digital magazine called the Annals of Improbable Research, shifted to Europe after 35 years in the United States over concerns about attendees being able to get visas.

At a convention center in Zurich, Switzerland, research teams received a custom trophy resembling a cross between a mushroom and a human foot. Among them were Matilda Brindle and Stuart West from the University of Oxford and the Florida Institute of Technology's Catherine F. Talbot, who reconstructed the evolutionary history of kissing, and the late Dr. Tokuji Unno, who investigated the science of blowing one's nose.
Another research team buried 1,000 pairs of underwear in more than 25 countries to study how critters in the soil helped them decompose.

For future ceremonies, organizers plan to alternate between Zurich and other European countries. The 2027 ceremony will be held in the Belgian city of Antwerp. Previous iterations took place at Harvard University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Boston University, but there are no immediate plans to return to the U.S.
"During the past year, it has become unsafe for our guests to visit the country," Marc Abrahams, master of ceremonies and editor of the magazine, told The Associated Press in an email in March.
The Nobel Prizes, which have no relation to their cheekily named counterpart, will be announced at the start of October.

title: Christie Brinkley shares how she keeps her three adult children coming home
summary: Christie Brinkley reveals how she keeps all three adult children coming home and why losing both parents deepened her devotion to family time.
story: Christie Brinkley, star of ‘American Summer,’ explains why losing both parents made family time more precious and shares how she keeps her children close.
Christie Brinkley never really had to face an empty nest.
The actress and supermodel stars opposite Steve Guttenberg in "American Summer," a feel-good tribute to simpler times and family connections.
The 72-year-old told Fox News Digital those themes aren't just on-screen. They're values she's embraced in her own life, creating a home her three adult children can still return to.

The movie, which hit theaters Sept. 4, follows Guttenberg's character as he looks back on a formative childhood summer filled with baseball, first love and the disappearance of his U.S. Army father overseas.
CHRISTIE BRINKLEY HAS FANS MISTAKING SUPERMODEL FOR DAUGHTER IN NEW PHOTOS
Christie Brinkley's new movie, "American Summer, hit theaters Sept. 4. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"I have always been all about family, so I have built my life in a way that my kids. ... I want them independent," Brinkley said. "I want them out there living, doing whatever, but they always tend to come home on weekends, holidays. We all really are big on being together, and I love that.

Christie Brinkley and daughters Sailor Lee Brinkley-Cook and Alexa Ray Joel arrive at the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit 2017 launch event at Center415 Event Space in New York City Feb. 16, 2017. (GC Images)
"It's funny because a lot of moms on Instagram will ask me, 'How do you get your kids to come home so often? Mine are off and about,'" the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl shared.
"And I think it's just to always let them know they're always welcome back. They can bring their friends, that kind of thing."
Christie Brinkley's children — Alexa Ray Joel, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook and Sailor Brinkley-Cook — remain a central part of her life. (Getty Images)

The supermodel is often photographed alongside her three grown children — Alexa Ray Joel, 40, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook, 31, and Sailor Brinkley-Cook, 28 — whether they're walking red carpets or stepping out in coordinated looks. Brinkley said their close bond didn't happen by accident but was rooted in the example set by her own parents.
WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY SHARES SECRET TO KEEPING HER FAMILY CLOSE

After losing both of her parents less than two months apart in 2012, Brinkley said she no longer takes family time for granted. Her father, Don Brinkley, died July 14, followed by her mother, Marge Brinkley, on Sept. 9.

"I have always cherished my family time," Brinkley said. "And I think once you lose both of your parents, it becomes more precious because you know that there is a finite time to it. And right now, our family's smaller because I don't have my mom and dad."
Alexa Ray Joel and Christie Brinkley appear onstage at the Big Apple Circus in New York City Feb. 1, 2020. (Getty Images for Big Apple Circus)
Brinkley became visibly emotional before saying, "I always get choked up whenever I talk about them."
Christie Brinkley's parents attend a pageant in Hawaii, date unknown. (Corbis via Getty Images)

Guttenberg is no stranger to Brinkley's heartbreak. He became a caregiver for his father, Stanley Guttenberg, after he developed kidney failure, eventually training to help administer dialysis at home.

"I remember you telling me about your mom and dad, Christie, that you had a little house on your property, and they lived near you, right?" Guttenberg said. "Isn't that wonderful? How lucky you were and are to have them right there. It's priceless, right? ... The greatest thing in the world."
Family came first for Steve Guttenberg, who paused his acting career to help care for his father, Stanley Guttenberg. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"The best," Brinkley replied. "My parents were always, always so ready to be there for me. Good times, bad times, they were always there, and they always made an effort to be a family. And I think it's so important, and it has given me my happiest moments."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"American Summer" is described as a homage to families in small-town America. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

Family continues to be an essential part of Brinkley's life. She shared that Alexa Ray was preparing for a concert that night, while Jack planned to attend the premiere of "American Summer" alongside her.
For Brinkley, the movie's message extends beyond the screen. She believes audiences are craving stories that celebrate family.
Christie Brinkley and Sailor Brinkley Cook attend the Solving Kids Cancer Annual Hamptons Luncheon at Tutto II Giorno in Southampton, N.Y., on Aug. 4, 2025. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

"People want to put down their phone and speak to another human face to face," she said. "This [story] takes us back before there were cellphones. And I think that we're going to find people now putting down their cellphones more often and just connecting with loved ones.

"And that human connection, nothing can replace it. I find that whenever I light a little bonfire in the backyard or at the beach. I always say, 'This is it. This is free. This is simple. And you know what? This is as good as it gets.'
Steve Guttenberg and Christie Brinkley in a scene from "American Summer." (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"Just to be able to sit there by the crackling of the fire, the moon coming up, the stars sparkling, the birds chirping, the crickets coming on, the fireflies lighting — that's it," she continued. "That's the best. Slowing down the speed of life, human connections. ... I think those are things that we all want to feel again and again."
"It's better than any Ferrari," Guttenberg said.

Christie Brinkley poses with son Jack at the opening night arrivals for Michael Moore's "The Terms of My Surrender" on Broadway at the Belasco Theatre in New York City Aug. 10, 2017. (Bruce Glikas/FilmMagic)
Brinkley's love of simple pleasures doesn't stop with family gatherings. She's also an avid birdwatcher, a hobby she believes is making a comeback as more people look to unplug.

Christie Brinkley attends Best Friends Animal Society's The Spirit of the Sanctuary"benefit Aug. 24, 2026, at Jill Rappaport's Last Buck Ranch in Water Mill, N.Y. (Getty Images)

"I've always been a birdwatcher," she said. "On my Instagram, I have a bird feeder, and if you go back, you'll see lots and lots of pictures of the birds at my bird feeder. And I was just reading that birdwatching is back in full force for young people, too. People want to connect with nature. They want to get in nature, and it's all part of just that slowing down."

title: Jeff Foxworthy reveals how 'redneck' insult inspired decades of comedy
summary: Jeff Foxworthy reveals why he brought back his iconic "redneck" jokes after 20 years for his Fox Nation special "The Joke's on Me," streaming now.
story: Foxworthy was able to turn what should have been an insult into a ‘compliment’ by turning it into a ‘badge of honor.’
Jeff Foxworthy turned an insult into a compliment when someone criticized where he came from.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 67-year-old actor and comedian discussed his new stand-up special, "The Joke's on Me," and recalled the time someone called him a "redneck" and how he turned what was meant to be an insult into a compliment.
He explained that "one of the nicest compliments" someone once gave him was commending his ability to turn what "was supposed to be an insult ... into a badge of honor."
DAVE CHAPPELLE SAYS HE’S CONSIDERING REVISITING ‘CHAPPELLE’S SHOW’ DECADES AFTER WALKING AWAY
"I said, 'Well, that's cool, because when people get offended, they act like if you gave rednecks a billion dollars, they wouldn't be rednecks,'" he said.

"I said they would still be rednecks. They would just have bigger boats, bigger trucks. I mean, more things to shoot at. They're happy with who they are. And I've always got asked, ‘How do you come up with that?’ And I'm like. There's no research going on. It's my family and my friend group that trust me."
Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up routine. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)
Foxworthy first began telling jokes about rednecks in the late '80s, and found them to be successful, so he continued telling them, even closing his 1990 special with one.

He explained that "they were easy to remember" and said they would always "get a laugh." After telling the jokes on stage for a while, he "thought, well people are tired of this" and stopped telling them.
"The last time I did them onstage was during the Blue Collar Comedy Tour" in 2003, he said.
WATCH: Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up.

After more than 20 years of staying away from the jokes, Foxworthy felt like it was time to bring them back. He recalled telling the crowd, "I hadn't done these in 20 years, but I'm thinking about for this special, bringing them back.
"I said that because when I said that if you've ever peed in the pool, the entire audience went, 'You might be a redneck.' And I went, 'Oh, wow, this stuck to people's bones, you know?'" he said.
"And I say, ‘Well, what if I did some to close, if that was my first special, and all these years later, this is my last.’ It kind of seemed like a nice little way to put a bow on it."
Foxworthy brought jokes about rednecks back into his act after realizing they still resonated with his audience. (Gary Gershoff/Getty Images)
He then went back and looked at all the redneck jokes he had written over the years, "and pulled out a bunch of them" to try at his next gig at a comedy club.

"It was like, I never stopped doing them," he said. "It was like going back 35 years, which was really cool for me. It's like one of your babies. You bring it back out and people go, 'Oh, we still love it.'"
WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy explains why he stopped telling 'redneck' jokes

Foxworthy's latest comedy special, "The Joke's on Me" began streaming on Fox Nation in June. Unlike other comedy specials, this one gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at the joke-writing process that goes into creating a special.

The comedian told Fox News Digital he was inspired to create the unique special after watching a documentary about the Beatles and realizing that "seeing the process didn't take anything away from the finished product," but rather made it better "because you saw the struggle that went into creating that."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Foxworthy came up with the idea for his new special after watching a documentary about the Beatles. (Getty Images)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
When Fox Nation approached him with the offer to do a stand-up special, he pitched them the behind-the-scenes idea.

"I said, 'But if you're willing to try something different, if you will show me note cards in hand, going into a club on a Tuesday night or a Wednesday night and just throwing these thoughts out.' Because one of the things that still fascinates me after over 40 years about stand-up is I still don't know what people are gonna laugh at," he said.

"You would think after 40 years, I would know. Now, I'll go in there with an idea, 'Oh, this is really funny.' And then nobody laughs. Or I'll have a card where I think this is so stupid, I'm embarrassed to say it, and you throw it out there and everybody's beaten the tables laughing. And you're like, really? And, so, I wanted to show that. And Fox Nation was the first place that ever said, 'OK, we'll do it.'"
Foxworthy has hinted that this could be his last stand-up special but assures fans that doesn't mean he will never perform on a stage again.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Foxworthy hinted this may be his last stand-up special. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images for Beloved Benefit)
He told Fox News Digital he has reached a point in his life where the time he would rather spend with his grandkids or on his tractor.
WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy clears up his comments about retiring from stand-up

"I've been on the road nonstop," he added. "I laugh at my music friends when they say they're on tour. I said, 'Well, tour implies it stops. At some point,' I said, 'I've been on tour since 1984.' It just never stopped. I still love stand-up. I just don't know that I'm willing. And, to be honest, I'm not sure I can do anything any better than this, which just feels like a good place to stop."

title: Brooke Hogan threatens to expose family receipts in 'final warning'
summary: Brooke Hogan threatened to release screenshots after Linda Hogan accused her of tossing the family aside, escalating their public estrangement.
story: HGTV ‘Rock the Block’ contestant Brooke Hogan tells Fox News Digital about her grief and healing journey after her father’s death.
Brooke Hogan is warning her family that she has receipts, and she's prepared to use them.

The 38-year-old daughter of late wrestling legend Hulk Hogan fired back after her mother, Linda Hogan, publicly lamented their yearslong estrangement and accused Brooke of tossing her family aside "like trash."
"This 👌 close to breaking out some screenshots – which are ONE of the many reasons WHY," Brooke wrote over a screenshot of her mother's Facebook post from Aug. 30 shared to her Instagram Story.
BROOKE HOGAN SAYS ‘I COULD HAVE SAVED YOU’ IN HAUNTING REGRET AFTER HULK HOGAN’S DEATH
Brooke Hogan threatened to bring out the "receipts" as her bitter family feud with mother Linda Hogan erupted again. (Brooke Hogan Oleksy/Instagram )
"I don't take CONSTANTLY dragging my name through the mud lightly," she continued.
"The selective amnesia isn't gonna work."
Brooke ended the message with two words: "Final warning."
The latest flare-up came after Linda shared old family photos on Facebook while expressing her frustration over her fractured relationship with her daughter.
"I posted these wonderful photos of Brooke my daughter with me and my ex-husband her father and my mom and dad and really .. the whole family ! Brooke is loved," Linda wrote.
"We feel hurt every day that she just tosses us aside .... like trash," she continued. "I want to make sure she remembers how it really was .. and can really see how much she was adored and loved."
Brooke's response suggested she remembers their family history differently and is prepared to make private communications public if the criticism continues.
The mother and daughter's latest exchange is another chapter in a fractured family that has played out publicly for years.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Brooke Hogan with her brother, Nick Hogan, and parents Hulk Hogan and Linda Hogan. (Michael Loccisano/FilmMagic)
Brooke first became famous alongside her parents, Hulk and Linda, and younger brother, Nick Hogan, on the VH1 reality series "Hogan Knows Best," which premiered in 2005.
The show followed the wrestling superstar and his family while also documenting Brooke's budding music career and her father's protective approach to his teenage daughter.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
The family dynamic changed dramatically after Linda filed for divorce from Hulk in 2007 after more than two decades of marriage. Their divorce was finalized in 2009.
Years later, Brooke became estranged from both parents, but she has made clear that her reasons for cutting contact with her mother were separate from the issues she had with her father.
Brooke addressed the family rift directly in a lengthy Instagram statement on March 27, 2025, insisting she had not chosen one parent over the other.

"No contact with my mom has nothing to do with my dad, and no contact with my father has nothing to do with my mother," Brooke wrote. "I have completely separate reasons for going no contact with each of my parents."
HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED
In the same statement, Brooke made serious allegations about her childhood and family relationships.

"I have been EXTREMELY verbally and mentally abused since childhood," she alleged. "Sadly, it would frequently turn physical. And sometimes it's not by the person you would assume, abuse comes in all shapes and sizes."
Brooke did not identify a specific person in that portion of her statement.
The Hogan family at the 2004 Radio Music Awards in Las Vegas in October 2004. (Frank Micelotta/Getty Images)
She also claimed she had been put in the position of publicly defending behavior within her family before eventually questioning what she had been told.
"I've been asked to defend poor behavior to the public and have done so out of love. Only to find I was misinformed, manipulated, and lied to," she wrote.
"I longed for a normal family, but it never came to fruition. I've repeatedly held my hand out to help them, only to have them pull me into the darkness with them.
"I've set boundaries that were not respected, which turned into a 'no contact' situation."
Her comments came after Linda publicly discussed the family's troubles in March 2025, reigniting attention around their strained relationship.
The conflict marked a dramatic departure from the image viewers were introduced to two decades earlier on "Hogan Knows Best."
Brooke was a teenager when the series premiered, with the show following her budding music career, dating life and her father's famously protective parenting.
WWE LEGEND HULK HOGAN'S DEATH REPORT RELEASED
Brooke previously told Fox News Digital that, despite her strained relationship with her father, she loved him. (Acey Harper/Getty Images)
In the years that followed, the family relationships viewers once watched on television became increasingly strained, with some of those disputes eventually playing out in public.
Her relationship with her father received renewed attention after his death on July 24, 2025.
Hulk, born Terry Bollea, died at age 71 after being hospitalized for cardiac arrest.
Hulk was survived by Brooke and Nick, whom he shared with Linda, as well as his wife, Sky Daily.
Despite being estranged from her father when he died, Brooke made clear in an April interview with Fox News Digital that her love for him had never disappeared.

"I’m honest with him now, and I talk to him all the time, even if that seems like I’m a cuckoo bird," she told Fox News Digital. "If he showed up today, I would just be like, ‘I love you so much, and I wish you would have just let me in.’"
Brooke also offered rare insight into why their relationship had become strained before his death.
Brooke said that she wanted to "save" her father before his death. (John Parra/WireImage)

"[It's] tough because, obviously, my dad and I weren't really speaking prior to his death — not because I didn't love him. … It's that he had become a little bit calloused in the direction he was going in his life and the people he was surrounding himself with," she said.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"I am the daughter that wanted to save him. And it's kind of, like, you can try to save somebody and if they don't want to be saved … it's a tough position to be in."
Her comments to Fox News Digital echoed what Brooke had emphasized in her March 2025 statement. Distancing herself from her father did not mean she had sided with her mother or vice versa.

Fox News Digital's Stephanie Giang-Paunon contributed to this report.

title: Spencer Pratt rips George Clooney's 'woke scold lecture' after Amal's lavish Venice look
summary: Spencer Pratt calls out George Clooney and Amal Clooney over Venice Film Festival glamour, saying he will never tolerate a "woke scold lecture" from the couple.
story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts discuss George Clooney saying the United States government is run by the ‘least qualified people.’
Spencer Pratt is taking aim at George Clooney.
The former reality star, who delved into politics this year with a run for mayor of Los Angeles, pulled no punches when he took to social media Friday to criticize Clooney and his wife, Amal.

"$500M net worth George Clooney could’ve permanently housed 8 homeless people for the rest of their lives with the money he spent on a single-use dress for his wife at a 4 hour event," Pratt claimed on X.
SPENCER PRATT'S UNEXPECTED POLITICAL RISE FROM MTV VILLAIN TO KAREN BASS' CHALLENGER
Spencer Pratt ran for mayor of Los Angeles on the Republican ticket before conceding in June. (Gilbert Flores/Getty Images)
"I will never tolerate a woke scold lecture from these people. Just be an ostentatious celebrity and own it."
Along with his post, he shared a Page Six article detailing a look Amal wore to the Venice Film Festival, where the Clooneys have been spotted several times this week.
According to the outlet, she wore a custom look by Haider Ackermann for Tom Ford and a pair of earrings from Cartier that cost $149,000 and a Cartier diamond bracelet that runs for $225,000.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
George and Amal Clooney walk the red carpet at the Venice Film Festival. (Laurent Hou/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images; JB Lacroix/FilmMagic)

In addition to walking red carpets in Venice, Clooney has spoken publicly multiple times at the festival, including at the opening night ceremony, when he accepted the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement award.

"The first people that authoritarians tried to shut down are not politicians. They’re journalists who ask questions. They’re the artists who refuse simple answers; the filmmakers, writers, actors and musicians who insist that someone you never met is deserving of your empathy.

They remind us that a stranger is never a stranger, and that he might just be the hero in somebody else’s story."
George Clooney at the Hotel Excelsior Venice Lido pier during the 83rd Venice International Film Festival Sept. 3, 2026, in Venice, Italy. (Getty Images)

There was tons of violence. The capital was surrounded with tanks. We’ve had some other difficult times, but this is one of them.

"There’s a great word — kakistocracy — which is a country run by the least qualified people. I think maybe we have a kakistocracy right now, but we’ll get through it, and we will have an election in November that should be a check and balance. And then, in 2028, with any luck, we’ll have some restoration into some normalcy."
George and Amal Clooney walked the red carpet together at the screening of "Ink." (Daniele Venturelli/WireImage)

title: Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan among stars who left fame behind before returning to Hollywood
summary: From Rick Moranis to Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan, these Hollywood stars walked away from fame and made remarkable comebacks years later on screen.
story: Actor Jonathan Bennett tells Fox News Digital he’s excited about his ‘Mean Girls’ co-star Lindsay Lohan’s return to acting and discusses co-hosting ChristmasCon with Lacey Chabert.
Rick Moranis is stepping back into the spotlight after decades away from Hollywood, joining a growing list of stars who left fame behind and later returned.
The 73-year-old actor is taking on his first live-action part in nearly 30 years after walking away from the entertainment industry at the height of his career after a family tragedy.
Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet in "Spaceballs: The New One," the long-awaited sequel to Mel Brooks' 1987 cult classic science-fiction comedy movie, "Spaceballs."
'DEADPOOL' STAR ROB DELANEY REVEALS HOW LOSING 2-YEAR-OLD SON CHANGED HIS APPROACH TO FAME

Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan disappeared from Hollywood before making triumphant returns years later. (David Becker/Getty Images for CinemaCon; Dave Benett/WireImage; Jeff Spicer/Getty Images)

In July, Moranis made a rare public appearance to promote the sequel at San Diego Comic-Con, where he received a standing ovation when he appeared on stage wearing his character's signature massive black helmet. Moranis participated in a panel discussion alongside co-stars Daphne Zuniga, Josh Gad, Keke Palmer and Lewis Pullman, as well as director Josh Greenbaum and screenwriters Benji Samit and Dan Hernandez.
Zuniga is reprising her role as Princess Vespa, while other original stars who returned for the sequel include George Wyner as Colonel Sandurz, Bill Pullman as Lone Starr and Brooks as Yogurt.
During the panel, Moranis revealed what finally brought him back in front of the camera after his decades-long hiatus.
Moranis made a surprise appearance at the "Spaceballs: The New One" panel at Comic-Con International: San Diego in July. (Variety via Getty Images)

"This came along right at the right time, and I started talking to these folks and hearing who was going to be in it," Moranis said, via People. "I spoke to Josh Greenbaum, and I heard that Bill Pullman was coming back, and that Lewis was going to be in it too. And it just felt like this is it. It’s time and — yes. I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made."

Moranis became one of Hollywood's most recognizable comedy stars in the 1980s and 1990s after starring in a string of hit movies, including "Spaceballs," "Ghostbusters," "Little Shop of Horrors," "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," "Parenthood," "My Blue Heaven" and "The Flintstones."

However, after his wife, costume designer Ann Belsky, died in 1991 after a battle with breast cancer, Moranis stepped away from show business to focus on raising their two children, daughter Rachel and son Mitchell. He last appeared on-screen in 1997's "Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves," the third installment in the "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids" movie series.
Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet. (Alamy)
During a 2015 interview with the Hollywood Reporter, Moranis reflected on his decision to prioritize his family over his career.

"I was working with really interesting people, wonderful people," he said. "I went from that to being at home with a couple of little kids, which is a very different lifestyle. But it was important to me. I have absolutely no regrets whatsoever. My life is wonderful."
Moranis also clarified that he had not officially retired from acting, telling the outlet, "I took a break, which turned into a longer break."

"But I’m interested in anything that I would find interesting," he continued. "I still get the occasional query about a film or television role and as soon as one comes along that piques my interest, I'll probably do it.
MATT DAMON SAYS HOLLYWOOD'S 'RUTHLESS' NATURE HAS TAKEN HIM AWAY FROM FATHERHOOD MORE THAN HE'D LIKE
"I’m happy with the things I said yes to, and I’m very happy with the many things I’ve said no to," Moranis added. "Yes, I am picky, and I’ll continue to be picky. Picky has worked for me."
One of Rick Moranis' final on-screen roles was in "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," in 1989. (AJ Pics/Alamy Stock Photo)

Though Moranis left live-action films behind for many years, he continued working occasionally as a voice actor. He first dipped his toe back into the movie business in 2001, voicing two characters in "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer & the Island of Misfit Toys." Some of his other voice-acting gigs include "Brother Bear," "The Animated Adventures of Bob & Doug McKenzie" and the voice of Dark Helmet in "The Goldbergs."

During his appearance at Comic-Con, Moranis once again set the record straight regarding the perception that he had retired as he revealed that he and Brooks had long discussed making a follow-up to "Spaceballs."
"Actually, I started talking to Mel about the sequel in 1989," he said. "We kept talking about it.
"I really wasn’t retired; I was just negotiating."
STOCKARD CHANNING HITS FIRST RED CARPET IN 2 YEARS AFTER SAYING SHE'S A 'RECLUSE'

While Moranis’ return has drawn renewed attention due to his decades-long absence, other stars have also taken long breaks from Hollywood before making high-profile comebacks. Here's a look at several celebrities who stepped away from the spotlight for years before finding their way back to the screen.
Cameron Diaz
Cameron Diaz returned to Hollywood after stepping away from acting in 2014. (Getty Images)
Cameron Diaz was one of Hollywood’s most bankable stars when she quietly stepped away from acting in 2014.

Diaz made her breakthrough in 1994's "The Mask" and went on to star in a series of hit films, including "There’s Something About Mary," "My Best Friend's Wedding," "Charlie's Angels," "My Sister's Keeper," "Shrek" and "The Other Woman," among others.
After starring in 2014's "Annie," Diaz walked away from show business to focus on building a life with husband Benji Madden.

"It felt like the right thing for me to reclaim my own life, and I just really didn't care about anything else," the actress said during a 2025 appearance at Fortune's Most Powerful Women Summit, according to E! News.

"Nobody's opinion, nobody's success, no one's offer, no one's anything could change my mind about my decision of taking care of myself and building the life that I really wanted to have. I think it really comes to what are you passionate about? For me, it was to build my family."
During her break, Diaz welcomed daughter Raddix, 6, and son Cardinal, 2, with Madden and launched her Avaline wine brand. The couple's third child, son Nautus, was born in May.

After a decade away from movies, Diaz returned to the screen in Netflix’s 2025 action comedy "Back in Action," starring opposite Jamie Foxx. She has since lined up other projects, including Netflix’s "Bad Day," Apple TV+’s "Outcome" and "Shrek 5," in which she will reprise her voice role as Princess Fiona.
Lindsay Lohan
Lindsay Lohan mounted a comeback years after fleeing Hollywood for Dubai. (Todd Owyoung/NBC via Getty Images)
Lindsay Lohan’s comeback followed years of intense public scrutiny and a long stretch away from major studio films.
Lohan became one of Hollywood’s biggest young stars after breaking out in "The Parent Trap" and later leading hits including "Freaky Friday," "Mean Girls" and "Herbie: Fully Loaded."

However, Lohan's promising career was derailed by multiple box-office flops and a string of highly-publicized legal problems and substance abuse issues. After years of tabloid attention and personal struggles, Lohan left the United States in 2014 and eventually relocated full-time to Dubai, spending much of the next decade outside the Hollywood spotlight. She told Emirates Woman in 2018 that moving to Dubai afforded her "a fresh start."

Lohan began rebuilding her acting career with Netflix’s 2022 holiday movie "Falling for Christmas," followed by more streaming projects and a major return to one of her signature roles in "Freakier Friday."

During a 2025 interview with The Sunday Times, Lohan said she stepped away because she had lost her excitement for making movies and wanted "a more private life, a real life," before returning once she felt "that itch again."
Lohan will next be seen in Hulu’s "Count My Lies," a limited series in which she stars opposite Shailene Woodley and Kit Harington.
Ke Huy Quan
Ke Huy Quan's comeback culminated in a Best Supporting Actor Oscar win. (Alberto Rodriguez/Variety via Getty Image)
Ke Huy Quan’s Hollywood disappearance ended with one of the industry’s most celebrated comeback stories.

Quan became a child star after playing Short Round opposite Harrison Ford in 1984’s "Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom" and Data in 1985’s "The Goonies." However, Ke only landed a few minor TV and film roles after his early fame and found himself being offered stereotypical parts geared toward Asians.

During a 2023 interview with People, Quan said he made the "very difficult decision" to walk away from acting in the early 2000s. He then spent years working behind the camera as a stunt coordinator and assistant director.
However, he recalled that, after seeing 2018’s "Crazy Rich Asians," he was inspired to revisit his first love.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"I was happy working behind the camera, but I had serious FOMO (fear of missing out)," Ke told the outlet. "I wanted to be up there with my fellow Asian actors."

After roughly two decades away from acting, Quan returned in 2022’s "Everything Everywhere All at Once," a role that earned him the Academy Award for best supporting actor. In his emotional Oscars speech, Quan reflected on his unlikely journey, saying, "Dreams are something you have to believe in. I almost gave up on mine."
Daniel Day-Lewis
Daniel Day-Lewis returned to Hollywood to team up with his son Ronan for 2025's "Anemone." (Jason Merritt/WireImage)
Daniel Day-Lewis has stepped away from Hollywood more than once, but his latest return marked the end of what many believed was a permanent retirement.

Known for his intensely selective approach to roles, Day-Lewis has previously taken long breaks throughout his career. After starring in 1997’s "The Boxer," Day-Lewis retreated from acting and spent several years in Italy learning shoemaking before returning in Martin Scorsese’s 2002 film, "Gangs of New York."

The three-time Oscar winner announced he was retiring from acting after starring in 2017’s "Phantom Thread." At the time, his representative said, "Daniel Day-Lewis will no longer be working as an actor. He is immensely grateful to all of his collaborators and audiences over the many years. This is a private decision and neither he nor his representatives will make any further comment on this subject."
Eight years later, his son, Ronan Day-Lewis, persuaded him to co-write and star in the 2025 drama "Anemone."
Day-Lewis later pushed back on the idea that he ever meant to permanently retire.

In a 2025 Rolling Stone interview, Day-Lewis said he "never intended to retire, really" and called his earlier retirement announcement "grandiose gibberish." He explained that he still loved the work but struggled with the lifestyle around filmmaking and felt "hollowed out" after "Phantom Thread."

He said returning for "Anemone" was largely about working with Ronan, who directed the film. Day-Lewis said that collaboration brought the spark back, saying, "Working with Ro, that furnace just lit up."
Renée Zellweger
Renee Zellweger took a six-year break from acting. (Getty Images)
Renée Zellweger stepped away from Hollywood after years of working at a relentless pace.

Zellweger became one of the most prominent actresses of the late 1990s and 2000s with roles in the hit movies "Jerry Maguire," "Bridget Jones’s Diary," "Chicago," "Cold Mountain" and "Cinderella Man." But after 2010’s "My Own Love Song," Zellweger took a six-year break from acting.
During a 2025 interview with British Vogue, Zellweger explained why she decided to pause her career.

"I was sick of the sound of my own voice. When I was working, I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, listen to you. Are you sad again, Renée? Oh, is this your mad voice?’ It was a regurgitation of the same emotional experiences," she said.
Zellweger told the outlet that her hiatus from acting enabled her to pursue other projects and embrace a healthier lifestyle.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I wrote music and studied international law," she said. "I built a house, rescued a pair of older doggies, created a partnership that led to a production company, advocated for and fundraised with a sick friend and spent a lot of time with family and godchildren and driving across the country with the dogs. I got healthy."

Zellweger returned in 2016 with the hit sequel "Bridget Jones’s Baby." She went on to earn some of the strongest reviews of her career for playing Judy Garland in 2019’s "Judy," and her performance earned her the Academy Award for best actress. Zellweger previously won the best supporting actress Oscar for her performance in "Cold Mountain."
Macaulay Culkin
Macaulay Culkin stepped away from acting as a teenager after childhood fame. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic)
Macaulay Culkin walked away from Hollywood after becoming one of the most famous child stars in the world.

Culkin shot to superstardom as Kevin McCallister in 1990’s "Home Alone" and its 1992 sequel, "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York." He went on to star in hit films, including "My Girl," "The Good Son" and "Richie Rich."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
After filming "Richie Rich," Culkin stepped away from acting, later explaining that he wanted to attend school, date and spend time with people his own age.

He returned nine years later with "Party Monster" and has continued accepting occasional projects on his own terms, including roles in "Saved!," "American Horror Story: Double Feature" and "The Righteous Gemstones."
Pamela Anderson
Pamela Anderson embraced a quieter lifestyle before her career reinvention. (Getty Images)
Pamela Anderson’s return to the spotlight has become one of Hollywood’s more unexpected late-career reinventions.

Anderson became a global sex symbol in the 1990s through "Baywatch," Playboy and years of tabloid attention that often overshadowed her acting ambitions. After decades of being defined by her image and personal life, she retreated to Vancouver Island, embraced a quieter lifestyle and began reassessing the public persona that had followed her for much of her career.

Her comeback began with a wave of projects that allowed her to reclaim her own story, including the 2023 Netflix documentary "Pamela, a Love Story" and her memoir, "Love, Pamela."
She made her Broadway debut in "Chicago" in 2022 and earned some of the strongest reviews of her career for "The Last Showgirl," along with Golden Globe and SAG nominations.

title: Trump pardons Jay-Z associate Emory Jones after federal drug conviction
summary: Alice Marie Johnson revealed Trump granted clemency to 30 individuals, including Emory Jones, a Roc Nation executive and Jay-Z's longtime associate.
story: Jon Bon Jovi and Jay-Z said their hellos on the field ahead of the 2026 Super Bowl.
Emory Jones, longtime friend and business associate of Jay-Z, has been granted a pardon from President Donald Trump.

Jones, an executive with Jay-Z's Roc Nation, was sentenced to nearly 16 years in 2000 on federal drug charges. Thanks in part to a letter from the hip-hop mogul, his sentence was reduced by 37 months, but now Trump has given him a completely clean slate.

The news was shared this week by Alice Marie Johnson, who was pardoned by Trump in 2020 after being sentenced to life in prison on a nonviolent drug charge in 1996. She now works with the White House as the "pardon czar."
JELLY ROLL GRANTED PARDON BY TENNESSEE GOVERNOR IN CHRISTMAS SEASON CLEMENCY DECISION
Trump pardoned 30 individuals Sept. 3, including Jay-Z's friend and business associate, Emory Jones. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images; Kevork S. Djansezian/Getty Images)

"Yesterday was a powerful day for second chances," Johnson wrote on Instagram. title: Miss America contestant reveals surprising day job as Massachusetts police officer
summary: Ashlyn Mercier became the first police officer named Miss Massachusetts and now competes for the Miss America crown while serving her community.
story: Miss Massachusetts Ashlyn Mercier reveals what inspired her law enforcement career and why competing for Miss America sends a powerful message to young girls.
Ashlyn Mercier has spent her career wearing a badge. Now, she's hoping to wear one of the country's most coveted tiaras.

The Westborough, Massachusetts, police officer is competing in Miss America. The final competition takes place Sept. 6 at the Palm Beach County Convention Center in West Palm Beach, Florida. Mercier is also the first police officer to be named Miss Massachusetts.
"I think there's not one single look for what a female police officer is supposed to look like," Mercier told Fox News Digital.

"And if we say that there is, that's just wrong because, at the end of the day, yes, female law enforcement officers only make up approximately 14% of the force in the United States, but we don't have to look a certain way.
NAVY VETERAN TRADES MILITARY UNIFORM FOR MISS GEORGIA SASH FOLLOWING HEARTBREAKING LOSS
Ashlyn Mercier, a police officer for the town of Westborough, Mass., is competing in the Miss America pageant. The final competition takes place Sept. 6, 2026. (Miss America)

"People are so multifaceted, women are so multifaceted and I'm just trying to show young girls that they can chase all of their dreams simultaneously," Mercier said. "They don't have to pick one thing and make that their entire identity."

The glitzy competition dates to a 1921 beauty contest in Atlantic City, New Jersey, held a year after the 19th Amendment guaranteed women the right to vote. The organization awards scholarships and gives its titleholder a national platform for community service and advocacy.

According to the Miss America organization, more than $300,000 in tuition scholarships will provide delegates "with meaningful support as they pursue their education and continue making an impact in communities across America." (Miss America)

Mercier hopes to raise awareness of her cause, Nick's Courage: One Smile Goes a Mile, named after her younger brother, Nicholas, a two-time pediatric cancer survivor. The initiative aims to bring positivity and hope to children battling critical illnesses.
In 2025, she took a year off from pageant competition to follow in her father's footsteps and attend the police academy.
WATCH: ACTIVE-DUTY POLICE OFFICER COMPETES IN MISS AMERICA

"I didn't know if I would ever come back and compete," Mercier said. "I was afraid of what other people would think if I chased both of those dreams at the same time. I also had this dream of becoming a police officer. But what I came to realize is that I can't worry about what other people think. I've got to focus on myself. And it ended up working out for me."
Mercier said the Westborough Police Department has been cheering her on as she balances the competition with her work as an officer. Fox News Digital reached out to the department for comment.
Ashlyn Mercier graduated from the police academy in 2025. (Miss America)

"I'm really fortunate that they have been so incredibly supportive," Mercier said. "I work for an amazing department, and my co-workers have supported me 100% from the moment I told them I was competing as Miss Massachusetts to now being at Miss America. They've shown up to my sendoff parties. They've helped me with my fundraising efforts. They've sent me good luck texts.
Ashlyn Mercier told Fox News Digital that fellow female officers have been cheering her on. (Miss America)
"It's really just an honor to be surrounded by people who uplift me," she said. "It really continues to help motivate me to move forward."

Mercier said her career in law enforcement doesn't give her an advantage on the Miss America stage. She's one of the delegates representing the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, each hoping to stand out.
Ashlyn Mercier started dispatching for the Westborough Fire Department. (Miss America)
Still, other officers have taken notice.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Ashlyn Mercier made history as the first police officer to win the state crown. (Miss America)
"I've had thousands of female law enforcement officers across the country commenting on my posts saying that they're rooting for me and that they're inspired by me," Mercier said.

"There are also young girls saying that they want to get into law enforcement, and they're inspired by my story. And then I serve my community in Westborough every single day in my capacity as a police officer, but I also get to serve my community in the role as Miss Massachusetts.
Ashlyn Mercier is highlighting Nick's Courage in honor of her younger brother. (Miss America)

"Those two things are what is so important about the Miss America opportunity," Mercier said. "Yes, we get to dress up. Yes, we get to wear pretty gowns and look beautiful. But women's empowerment and service are the core. And if you look at it like that, you can see and draw a lot of parallels between Miss America and between my role as Officer Mercier."

Police work has also given Mercier skills she can use in the competition. She said she's comfortable communicating with different people and staying calm in nerve-wracking situations. But one challenge remains.
Ashlyn Mercier was named Miss Massachusetts 2026. (Miss America)
When asked whether getting ready for a shift or a pageant takes longer, she didn't miss a beat.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Ashlyn Mercier is a second-generation police officer. (Miss America)

"Oh, absolutely getting ready for a pageant," she said with a laugh. "I do not look like this on a daily basis when I go to work. I'll have maybe some mascara on, and the hair gets slicked back in a bun. I've got that down in about two minutes flat. This definitely takes a lot longer."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Ashlyn Mercier's father is a corporal with the Oxford Police Department. (Miss America)
This year's competition commemorates 105 years of Miss America. Whether she earns the title or not, Mercier said she's determined to use her platform to make a difference.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Ashlyn Mercier hopes to inspire young girls to pursue a career in law enforcement. (Miss America)

"If I do win, I just hope to be an inspiration to young women and girls looking up to [me], knowing that she can be a police officer, and she can be Miss America," Mercier said. "She can chase all her dreams at once. I've been told I should pick one, focus on one. But you can do it all. My message is to inspire the next generation."

title: Donna Mills does 100 sit-ups a day, plays tennis five times a week at 85 but won't quit Doritos
summary: Donna Mills revealed her grueling daily fitness routine and confessed to a Doritos "addiction" she's carried through her decades-long career.
story: The longtime Hollywood actress tells Fox News Digital how she keeps her body moving with a demanding fitness regimen.
Donna Mills is keeping fans on their toes at 85, from launching an OnlyFans account to revealing the intense fitness routine she credits with keeping her active.

The former ballerina, best known for playing the scheming Abby Cunningham on "Knots Landing," revealed to Fox News Digital the demanding fitness routine she credits with keeping her moving — including 100 sit-ups, 50 leg lifts, up to an hour on the bike and, sometimes, tennis five days a week.
And while Mills has long been disciplined about her health — including cutting out sugar — there is one indulgence she refuses to completely give up.
'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS SAYS REFUSING TO POSE NUDE COST HER PLAYBOY COVER
American actress Donna Mills as she performs barre exercises in her home dance studio, Beverly Hills, California, March 18, 1983. (Bob Riha, Jr./Getty Images)

"I mean, it’s not good for you. It’s not. You know, I know I shouldn’t do it," Mills admitted.
WATCH: 'Knots Landing' star Donna Mills swears by this daily routine at 85
Still, she said the popular snack has followed her throughout her decades-long career.

"Different sets that I’ve been on… for some reason, they know — they always got a bag of Doritos in the trailer for me… it’s really funny. But I’ve never lost that. I don’t eat them as much as I used to. But they’re still a treat."
Mills as she performs exercises in her home dance studio, March 18, 1983. (Getty Images)
When it comes to exercise, Mills' routine is considerably more demanding.
"I started out as a dancer, so a ballerina. I mean, I was on pointe, the whole thing," she said.
'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS ISSUES URGENT WARNING ABOUT AGING
Mills said her early training instilled a work ethic that has stuck with her throughout her life.
"So that gave me a discipline that most people don’t have because ballet is very hard," she explained.
Mills starred in the TV soap opera series "Knots Landing," in June 1980. (Getty Images)
To this day, she still incorporates elements of her early training into her workouts.

"I do 100 sit-ups a day, 50 leg lifts, lots of stretching. I have a ballet barre in my little gym."
Her rigorous routine doesn’t stop there.
"And ride the bike for about 45 minutes or an hour," she continued.

She also stays active on the court whenever she can.
"I play tennis five times a week sometimes. And so that’s very, very important."
The Hollywood actress takes a similarly disciplined approach to her diet, saying a book she read years ago influenced her decision to cut back on sweets.
"I’ve always been anti-sugar," she said. "I read a book a long time ago called 'Sugar Blues' that really talked about the sugar industry and everything, and I have stayed away from it ever since."
Donna Mills stays active at 85 with daily sit-ups and tennis several times a week. (Photo by Tim P. Whitby)
Still, Mills isn't pretending her lifestyle is effortless.
"It’s a lot of stuff. You got to work at it."
'PERFECT' WORKOUT FORMULA CAN TAKE JUST 10 MINUTES A DAY, HILARIA BALDWIN SAYS
Her fitness routine comes as Mills enters what she describes as an entirely new chapter of her life.
The actress launched an OnlyFans account at 85, embracing a platform she initially knew nothing about.

Mills has already seen major interest in her new venture, with Creators Inc. telling her she’s doing "incredibly well" and bringing in "many six figures" early on.
But money isn't the only draw. Mills said fans are hungry for a behind-the-scenes look at her life — something she said wasn't possible during her TV heyday.

"They want to know me. They want to know what I do during the day when I’m home. They want to see my home. They want to know much more about my personal life than we ever experienced back in the ’80s and the ’90s that, you know, the fans were cut off from."
Now, they’re "invited in" — potentially even to Mills’ vineyard.
Her OnlyFans audience has already made some unusual requests, including one involving barefoot grape-stomping.

"I said I would do the photo shoot for Playboy if they were okay with the fact that I wasn’t going to show anything," she recalled.
But she said the photographer continued pushing her boundaries throughout the three-day shoot. Mills insisted the photos didn't need nudity to make an impression.
"They’re very sexy," she exclaimed.

The "Knots Landing" star keeps fit with 100 daily sit-ups and frequent tennis as she turns up the heat on OnlyFans. (Maureen Donaldson / Michael Ochs Archives / Getty Images; Unique Nicole / Getty Images)

Now, she's bringing those images and her personality directly to fans.

For Mills, the point isn't simply launching a provocative new platform. It's proving that getting older doesn't mean life gets smaller.
