Melcher had previously declined to sign Manson to a recording contract.

"The murder is tried to be made to look like it was part of Gary Hinman’s murder," said Berlinger. "But when Manson picks up the paper the next day, and there’s no information about these two murders being linked, they do another murder. The logic is, ‘We’ve got to make people think that Bobby, who is sitting in prison, is not guilty.’"

Charles Manson travels in a police van to the Santa Monica Courthouse to appear in court for a hearing regarding the murder of music teacher Gary Hinman in Los Angeles, California on June 25, 1970. (Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)
"This was all a series of blunders, a bunch of bad, spontaneous decision-making."

The next night, wealthy grocer Leno LaBianca and his wife, Rosemary LaBianca, were stabbed and killed in their home across town. The killers scrawled phrases including "Pigs" and the misspelled words "Healter Skelter" in blood at the crime scene.

Prosecutors maintained at trial that Manson ordered his followers to kill some of Los Angeles' rich and famous to trigger a race war, a plan prosecutors said grew in part from his interpretation of the Beatles' song "Helter Skelter."
Manson family members Susan Atkins, Patricia Krenwinkle and Leslie van Houton. (Bettmann Archive)

Manson frequently spoke about an impending race war and interpreted songs on the Beatles' "White Album" as messages about the coming conflict, according to testimony from his followers. What remains disputed is whether those beliefs motivated the Tate-LaBianca murders or whether, as Berlinger argues, prosecutors elevated them into the central theory of their case.

Deputy District Attorney Vincent Bugliosi talks to journalists outside the courtroom after the jury decreed the death penalty for Charles Manson and three female followers in the Tate-LaBianca murders of August 1969. (Bettmann Archive)

"[Prosecutor Vincent Bugliosi] had to come up with a legal theory to convict a guy who actually didn’t do the killings," Berlinger said. "Manson wasn’t even there when the Tate-LaBianca killings took place. So how do you convict somebody who wasn’t there? Well, you come up with this organizing principle that he convinced his followers that a race war was coming, and he was trying to make that race war happen. It was a brilliant legal theory, but it’s a false story."
"The Manson murders are much more tragic, but much more banal than this idea of some crazy cult trying to start a race war," Berlinger continued.

"This was a drug deal gone bad, trying to cover up Gary Hinman’s killing by doing another murder the next day to make it look like a copycat murder, which were the Tate murders. Bugliosi worked with writer Curt Gentry on a book about the case. Published in 1974, "Helter Skelter" became the bestselling true crime book of all time.
The book "Helter Skelter" by Vincent Bugliosi and Curt Gentry, photographed on Jan. 10, 2014, in New York City. (Getty Images)

Manson and three followers — Susan Atkins, Patricia Krenwinkel and Leslie Van Houten — were found guilty and later sentenced to death. Charles "Tex" Watson was tried separately and convicted later. Charles Manson's 1969 mugshot. (Getty Images)

Manson died at a California hospital in 2017 while serving a life sentence. He was 83.

Berlinger maintained Manson's reputation as an evil mastermind was fueled more by myth than reality.

"He wasn’t killing or ordering people to kill to get some kind of satisfaction," Berlinger said. "He was covering up a series of blunders and just getting deeper and deeper into a hole. The best way to honor the victims is to be truthful about what happened."

title: ICE officer pleads not guilty to lying about Minneapolis shooting involving Venezuelan man
summary: Video evidence allegedly contradicted the ICE officer's claims about the Minneapolis shooting of Venezuelan man Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, prosecutors say.
story: Fox News correspondent Christina Coleman reports from Dallas on a federal judge blocking attempts by Minnesota to extradite ICE agent Christian Castro from Texas. Castro faces charges stemming from the January shooting of a Venezuelan migrant during Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis, while Texas Gov. Greg Abbott investigates whether the officer legally qualifies as a fugitive.

A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer pleaded not guilty Friday to charges of lying about a January shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis during the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration.

Christian Castro appeared in a Texas federal court where he faces six charges of making "materially false" statements to investigators, according to federal court documents unsealed Friday. He turned himself in to authorities Thursday evening.
A judge ordered Castro released on a $75,000 unsecured bond and required him to wear an ankle monitor.
DOJ CHARGES ICE OFFICER WITH LYING TO INVESTIGATORS FOLLOWING MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING OF VENEZUELAN MAN

Left: Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer Christian Castro gets into a car surrounded by news reporters moments after being released from the Carrizalez-Rucker Cameron County Detention Center in Brownsville, Texas on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026; Right: Christian Castro. (Left: AP Photo/Michael Gonzalez; Right: Cameron County Sheriff's Office)
The charges stem from the Jan. 14 shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan man who was shot in the leg. Moments earlier, Castro and his partner attempted to stop a vehicle.
The driver, also a Venezuelan citizen, fled, triggering a foot chase.

Castro caught up to the driver and a physical struggle ensued, according to the indictment. Sosa-Celis attempted to help the driver, and they both fled into a nearby apartment duplex and shut the door.
ICE AGENTS IN FATAL HOUSTON SHOOTING WERE NOT WEARING BODY CAMERAS, SOURCES SAY
Castro drew his service weapon and fired a single shot through the front door, striking Sosa-Celis in the leg, federal prosecutors said.
Two 1-year-old children and two women were inside the home when Castro opened fire, prosecutors added.

In an attempt to justify the shooting, Castro allegedly told investigators he was brutally assaulted by multiple individuals wielding tools, claiming he was hit with a broom and a snow shovel during the confrontation. He also claimed he was on his back when he fired toward the fleeing men, officials said.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT
FILE - U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents conduct immigration enforcement operations in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on Thursday, Jan. 28, 2026. (Madison Thorn/Anadolu via Getty Images)

However, video evidence later contradicted those statements, prompting an investigation. Federal prosecutors said Castro was standing up when he opened fire, and they disputed his claim that he fought the suspect on the ground for three minutes, noting the struggle actually lasted about 11 seconds.
The shooting occurred amid a targeted crackdown on illegal immigration in Minneapolis.
Castro faces separate charges in Minnesota and was previously arrested in Texas in May.

His case has sparked a legal battle involving Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who has refused to extradite him to Minnesota.

title: Illinois mother charged with murder in death of 2-year-old son in case drawing comparisons to Lindsay Clancy

story: Constitutional law attorney Jonathan Turley discusses Plymouth County Superior Court Judge William Sullivan declaring a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case after the jury remained deadlocked and the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court denied the defense's emergency appeal, breaking down the legal implications of the ruling, the prosecution's options moving forward and what to expect if the case heads to a second trial on 'America Reports.'
An Illinois woman has been charged with three counts of murder in the death of her 2-year-old son in a case that has already drawn comparisons to the Lindsay Clancy trial, authorities confirmed.

Corie A. Walsh, 40, was being held for medical treatment on Friday after she was found with wounds believed to be self-inflicted but non-life-threatening when police responded to her home Tuesday, the Frankfort Police Department said in a news release.

An investigator works behind police tape outside a Frankfort, Ill., home where a 2-year-old boy died. (FOX 32 Chicago)
Once she’s released from treatment, she will be transferred to the Will County Adult Detention Facility to await a hearing.
Frankfort police officers responded to Walsh’s home Tuesday afternoon and found her son unresponsive. He was given CPR and transported to a hospital where he was later pronounced dead.
Walsh was closely following the Clancy trial and was discussing the case in an online group chat as the jury deliberated just hours before her son was found, prosecutors said, according to FOX 32.

Lindsay Clancy listens to testimony at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., last month. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)

Carolyn Pappas, who lives nearby, told NBC Chicago earlier this week that the boy’s death has left residents stunned. title: First responders honor World Trade Center beam arriving at Boston fallen heroes memorial
summary: The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour brought a 21-foot World Trade Center beam to the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston.
story: The Tunnel to Towers tour made a stop in Boston with a section of World Trade Center steel.
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour honored fallen heroes in Boston Wednesday as part of a nationwide tour slated to finish in New York City just after Sept. 11.
The group brought a preserved 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower of the World Trade Center, which has been on tour since May, to the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston's Seaport.

"For us as first responders and veterans, what this means as we come up on the 25th anniversary is personal. It's all about educating the next generation and not forgetting the sacrifices, not only made on 9/11 but what we've endured in the 20 years after in all theaters of combat," said Dan Magoon, executive director of Massachusetts Fallen Heroes.
AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

Guests pay their respects Wednesday as they approach a 21-foot, 16,900-pound steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center's South Tower during the Steel Across America tour at the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston's Seaport. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories)

Mike Eruzione, captain of the 1980 U.S. Winter Olympics hockey team that won the historic "Miracle on Ice" game against the Soviet Union, honored his friends who were passengers on one of the hijacked planes involved in the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

"It touched the heart of our country. It touched the souls of our country," Eruzione said of Tunnel to Towers, which helps 9/11 families, first responders and veterans rebuild in part from funds raised through nationwide charity runs.

Guests stand in front of the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston Wednesday. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories)
The gathering brought together first responders from Massachusetts as well as law enforcement. Guests were allowed to approach the 16,900-pound beam and pay their respects.

"It's just crazy to think about where it once stood, the people that worked inside the buildings, the people that rushed inside to save those people and what happened when it all came down," said Daniel McCarthy, a Bostonian whose parents are from New York.
WHERE TUNNEL TO TOWERS' STEEL ACROSS AMERICA TOUR WILL STOP AHEAD OF 9/11
American flags on a grassy area at the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories)
The beam was brought to Fenway Park Wednesday night after traveling to the U.S. Military Academy at West Point Monday.

title: Lindsay Clancy mistrial declared after jury deadlocks in killings of her three children
summary: Lindsay Clancy's trial centered on whether severe mental illness relieved her of criminal responsibility in the January 2023 deaths of her three children.
story: Plymouth County Superior Court Judge William Sullivan declares a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case after the jury deadlocked and a defense appeal was denied.

Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Friday in Lindsay Clancy’s murder case after jurors said they were unable to reach a unanimous verdict in the killings of her three children after a week of deliberating at the Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts.

The mistrial followed a dramatic dispute over an alleged 11-1 divide, with Clancy’s defense arguing that the lone holdout juror had acknowledged doubt but was refusing to properly apply the court’s instructions on reasonable doubt.

The alleged holdout is believed to be one of the three male jurors on the 12-person panel after defense attorney Kevin Reddington repeatedly referred to the unnamed juror as a male inside and outside court.
POSTPARTUM MOM LINDSAY CLANCY ON TRIAL FOR MURDER BRINGS COURT TO A HALT WITH SUDDEN BREAKDOWN

"[The other jurors] know that they were robbed — by one man — for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful and listened to this evidence," he told reporters after leaving the courthouse.
"And you could see how defeated they were sitting there. And I got a funny feeling they could go one for another week if they had to. So, I hope that guy can sleep well at night."
Callan, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Mass., home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)

Also speaking outside the courthouse, Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz acknowledged the victims in this case — the Clancy children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan.
"It is our job to make sure the victims are not invisible," Cruz said. "I am a father and a grandfather, and I cannot imagine the hell this entire family has lived through."

Clancy’s attorneys made an emergency appeal to the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court in an attempt to stay the mistrial and force further inquiry into the juror. Justice Dalila Argaez Wendlandt denied the request Friday afternoon, clearing the way for Sullivan to formally declare the mistrial.
HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL
Clancy had been charged with first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths of her children, each of whom had been strangled with exercise bands.
The trial centered on whether she was legally responsible for her actions at the time, and the defense argued she wasn't due to postpartum psychosis.
Her attorneys argued that severe mental illness left her unable to appreciate the wrongfulness of what she was doing or unable to conform her conduct to the requirements of the law.
LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN
Lindsay and Patrick Clancy with two of their three children in an undated photo (Lindsay Marie Clancy/ Facebook)

Prosecutors maintained that Clancy remained criminally responsible and pointed to evidence they said showed planning, purposeful behavior and an awareness of what she was doing before, during and after the killings.

During the trial, Clancy's former husband, Patrick Clancy, testified about the day of the slayings, which happened while he was running errands that included picking up children's stool softener at a CVS store and takeout for dinner. They spoke on the phone while he was out.
Under Massachusetts law, once lack of criminal responsibility is properly raised, prosecutors must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that a defendant was criminally responsible.
Lindsay and Patrick Clancy with two of their three children in an undated photo (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
The mistrial means the case ended without a verdict, and Clancy was neither convicted nor acquitted. Prosecutors can seek to retry her but have not yet announced a decision.

Sullivan said he wants the case retried "sooner rather than later," suggesting a new trial could potentially take place later this fall. Clancy is due back in court Sept. 29 for a status hearing, trial assignment and a defense Rule 25 motion.
All previous bail orders remain in effect.
JUDGE SENTENCES NEVADA MOM FOR DROWNING YOUNG SON, DAUGHTER: 'I WILL REMEMBER YOUR CASE FOREVER'
Lindsay Clancy listens to testimony Aug. 10, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
The mistrial followed a trial that focused extensively on Clancy's psychiatric condition in the months and weeks before the children died.
Lindsay Clancy holding her youngest child, Callan, who was only 7 months old when he died.  (Lindsay Marie Clancy Facebook)
Jurors heard testimony about her treatment by mental health professionals, psychiatric medications, anxiety, depression, insomnia and other symptoms documented before the killings.

Attorney Kevin Reddington holds up a display board of a text message Lindsay Clancy sent her mother Paula during her murder trial in Plymouth Superior Court Aug. 26, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger/Pool via AP)
On Jan. 24, 2023, authorities responded to the Clancy family's Duxbury home after Patrick Clancy returned and found his wife seriously injured outside the house.

The couple's three children were found inside.
BROOKLYN MOTHER WHO DROWNED HER THREE CHILDREN IN THE OCEAN NEAR CONEY ISLAND SENTENCED TO DECADES IN PRISON

Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague rested her case as defense attorney Kevin Reddington asked rebuttal witness Dr. Gregory Saathoff one last question during the Lindsay Clancy murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., Aug. 26, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool The Patriot Ledger via AP)
Cora and Dawson died that night. Callan was taken to a hospital and died several days later.
Lindsay Clancy survived after jumping from a second-story window and suffered injuries that left her paralyzed in a wheelchair.
The prosecution and defense offered sharply different explanations for what happened before the children were killed.
Patrick Clancy and Rachel Danis hold hands as they walk through East Midtown in New York City, N.Y. Sept. 2, 2026.  (Elder Ordonez/InStar for Fox News Digital)

The defense had argued that the deaths occurred after months of worsening psychiatric symptoms and treatment and that Clancy's mental condition had deteriorated to the point she could not legally be held criminally responsible.

Specifically, the defense contended that Clancy heard a male voice that commanded her to kill her three children. Dr. Phillip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist, said it was almost as if she was a "puppet."

"Not only did she hear a command, but she felt that her body was taken over by an external force where she was in a dream state and did not have control of her own body. It was almost like she was a puppet, and someone else was pulling the strings," Resnick said.
However, prosecutors rejected that claim, and their experts argued Clancy deliberately created an opportunity to be alone with the children and intentionally killed them.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Lindsay Clancy listens to the testimony of Dr. Gregory Saathoff during her murder trial in Plymouth Superior Court Aug. 26, 2026 in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

Gregory Saathoff, a forensic psychiatrist at the University of Virginia who consults the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit, told jurors Clancy's self-described auditory hallucinations were "very unusual."

"What was significant to me is that she had not spoken about hearing voices before to any of the mental health professionals, psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, physicians and staff in the emergency department or at McLean," Saathoff said.

"This was the first time she reported that, and that she experienced an auditory hallucination, according to what she told me. So, that was unusual. And then what was very unusual was the fact that the voice stopped with the strangling of her youngest son."
During the trial, members of Clancy's family revealed they were "very concerned" about her mental health in the months before she killed her three kids.
Susan Clancy, Lindsay's mother-in-law, told jurors she was concerned about Lindsay's mental health during the holiday season in 2022 but said she was a caring mother.
"Lindsay was struggling. We were all very concerned," Susan Clancy said. "She was very nurturing, very loving. She was a wonderful mother. Wonderful.
"She was begging for help."

Susan Clancy, the former mother-in-law of Lindsay Clancy, testifies during Lindsay Clancy's murder trial in Plymouth Mass., Aug. 18, 2026 in Plymouth, Mass. (Jonathan Wiggs/The Boston Globe via AP, Pool)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Paula Musgrove, Lindsay Clancy's mother, also told jurors about the mental health problems. In an Oct. 20, 2022 text message, Lindsay Clancy asked her mother for help.

"Mom, will you please come up and stay with me for a bit? I'm really sick. Something is wrong. I had horrible insomnia all night, and I just don’t know how I am going to get through the day. ... It’s just really scary, and I don’t want to be alone," the text read.
Fox News' Michelle Langer and Maria Paronich contributed to this report.

title: West Virginia principal suspended after recording devices found in girls’ locker rooms
summary: The Brooke County principal faces two felony charges and is being held on $100,000 bond after officials reportedly found devices at the school and his home.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
School administrators immediately suspended a West Virginia high school principal Wednesday after officials reportedly discovered recording devices placed in multiple locker rooms.
The criminal investigation involves Eric James, 53, who served as principal of Brooke High School in Wellsburg.
Officials said four devices were found in the female physical education locker rooms, including a separate locker room and another dressing area used by the school's dance team, according to WTOV 9.

title: Former North Texas police officer given three life sentences for child pornography, solicitation of minor
summary: A North Texas jury convicted Daniel Joseph Bates after he claimed 300-plus explicit child images were part of a secret human trafficking investigation.
story: Collin County District Attorney Greg Willis and prosecutor Bill Wirksye react to Karmelo Anthony's 35-year murder sentence, emphasizing the jury's focus on evidence. They clarify jury selection, discuss the community's response and address Anthony's appeal, underscoring that the case was never about race despite outside narratives.

A former police officer in North Texas was ordered to serve three consecutive life sentences in prison after investigators found him in possession of over 300 videos and images of children being sexually abused, according to a statement from Johnson and Somerville Counties' district attorney.

Former Itasca Police Department Officer Daniel Joseph Bates was convicted Wednesday of possession of child pornography and online solicitation of a minor after a civilian set him up in an entrapment scheme, according to a statement District Attorney Timothy Good shared with Fox News Digital.
Texas Rangers arrested Bates after an adult decoy posing as a 15-year-old girl alerted police that Bates was communicating with someone he believed to be a minor, according to the statement.

The civilian alerted police to Bates' communications with him, prompting Rangers to obtain a search warrant for his digital devices, and they allegedly found over 300 images of minor children being sexually abused, according to the statement.
NEW MISSISSIPPI LAW EXPANDS DEATH PENALTY TO INCLUDE INMATES ON CHILD SEXUAL BATTERY CONVICTIONS

title: ICE lodges detainer for illegal immigrant charged in wrong-way Maryland crash that killed mom, daughter
summary: ICE lodged a detainer for Jose Antonio Caballero-Nolasco, an El Salvador immigrant charged with killing a mother and daughter in a wrong-way crash.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

FIRST ON FOX: An illegal immigrant from El Salvador charged with killing a mother and her daughter while driving drunk the wrong way on a Maryland freeway is being sought by federal immigration authorities.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has lodged a detainer request with authorities in Montgomery County for Jose Antonio Caballero-Nolasco, the Department of Homeland Security told Fox News Digital.
He is charged with two counts of grossly negligent manslaughter, two counts of homicide by motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol, and life-threatening injury by a motor vehicle.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED POLICE OFFICER AND HIS GIRLFRIEND
Split of Interstate 270 and Jose Antonio Caballero-Nolasco. (DHS; Sarah L. Voisin/The Washington Post via Getty Images)
ILLEGAL ALIEN CHARGED WITH KILLING 4 YOUNG PEOPLE IN WRONG-WAY DUI CRASH ON OKLAHOMA HIGHWAY
Officials said Caballero-Nolasco was under the influence while driving the wrong way on Interstate 270 on Aug. 29, right before he crashed head-on into a vehicle with four people inside.

Two of the occupants, Musammat Shamima Begum, 46, and her 23-year-old daughter Areebah Jahin, were killed. They were from Northern Virginia and were on their way home at the time of the crash, affiliate FOX 5 D.C. reported.
Two others, a 62-year-old man and an 8-year-old girl, survived and were taken to local hospitals.
Investigators said they believe that alcohol impairment was a contributing factor in the crash.
FILE - DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the tragedy was "completely avoidable." (Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
ICE ARRESTS RELEASED ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF KILLING DAUGHTER, 9, IN ARIZONA ROLLOVER CRASH

"This tragedy was completely avoidable. Musammat Shamima Begum and Areebah Jahin should still be alive. ICE has lodged a detainer asking officials in Maryland to commit to not releasing this killer back onto our streets," said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. "My thoughts and prayers are with the victims and their family, and for a swift recovery for those who were injured."

Responding officers at the scene of the crash said Caballero-Nolasco smelled of alcohol, had bloodshot eyes, and slurred speech after the crash. He did not show any signs of braking before the crash, FOX 5 reported.

"There were some beer bottles that he admitted that he had been drinking," said Montgomery County State’s Attorney John McCarthy. "There were other bottles that were empty and full bottles were found within the vehicle."

Caballero-Nolasco was taken to a local hospital before being transferred to the Montgomery County Detention Center.

title: Rock concert at Virginia's Wolf Trap canceled after worker is crushed to death beneath tour bus
summary: A tour bus support apparatus failed at Wolf Trap National Park, crushing a worker underneath, hours before Squeeze was set to perform Thursday.
story: A rock show at the Wolf Trap performing arts venue was canceled after a man was crushed by the tour bus he was working underneath.
A rock performance at a venue in Virginia was canceled Thursday after a man working on a tour bus in a nearby parking lot was crushed underneath it hours before the show, according to authorities.
U.S. Park Police told FOX 5 DC they responded to the Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts at 5 p.m.
The English rock band "Squeeze" was scheduled to perform at 7:30 p.m. that night.
The worker was under the tour bus when officers arrived. Park Police said a supporting apparatus failed, causing the bus to come down on him.
An overhead view of the tour bus that collapsed onto a worker on Sept. 3, 2026, in a parking lot near the Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts in Virginia before a rock concert. (FOX 5 DC)
CONNECTICUT DAD JUMPED TO HIS DEATH DURING CONCERT AT MADISON SQUARE GARDEN IN NYC: REPORT
"There was an accident involving a member of the community at Wolf Trap National Park," the venue said in a social media post. "Out of respect, tonight's show has been canceled."

"Squeeze are deeply saddened and shocked by an incident that occurred at the venue earlier today, which resulted in the loss of a life," the band said in a statement to Rolling Stone. "We will work with the promoter and venue regarding the possibility of rescheduling the show and will communicate further information to ticket holders as soon as it is available. Our thoughts remain with everyone affected by this tragic event."
Simon Hanson and Glenn Tilbrook of Squeeze perform live on stage at Hard Rock Live in the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Sept. 22, 2021, in Hollywood, Fla. (Johnny Louis/Getty Images)
COUNTRY STAR MARK CHESNUTT'S LONGTIME BANDMATE DIES UNEXPECTEDLY ON TOUR BUS
The worker's identity has not been released by Park Police.
News of the accident prompted some fans to leave, but many lingered in the parking lot, shaken by the death of the worker.

"It was horrible when we found out that happened," Debbie Daniel told FOX 5 DC. "We saw the emergency vehicles come in, figured something serious had happened because there was like 15 or more vehicles. But, yeah, it was very tragic."
Concertgoers at the Wolf Trap who stuck around in the parking lot after the worker's death was announced on Sept. 3, 2026. (FOX 5 DC)

Eric Anderson, another fan, empathized with the man's colleagues and agreed with the decision to cancel the show.

title: Coast Guard recovers 47 bales of suspected marijuana worth $2.4M after intercepting go-fast vessel
summary: The U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba intercepted a suspicious go-fast vessel and recovered 47 bales of suspected marijuana worth over $2.4 million.
story: U.S. Southern Command video shows Marines and sailors interdicting and boarding a vessel allegedly used as a floating refueling station for the Los Choneros drug trafficking organization before U.S. forces sank it.
The U.S. Coast Guard recovered more than a ton of suspected marijuana worth over $2.4 million after crews intercepted a suspicious go-fast vessel during a patrol, military officials said.
Crews recovered 47 bales weighing a combined 2,082 pounds along the vessel's previous route, according to Joint Interagency Task Force South (JIATF-S).
Four people were detained in connection with the operation, JIATF-S said.
Officials said the seizure happened during a routine patrol after the crew of U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba detected "a suspicious go-fast vessel" and launched a boat crew to investigate.
NEWLY UNCLASSIFIED PENTAGON IMAGES SHOW SUSPECTED DRUG BOATS AS OFFICIAL ISSUES DEADLY WARNING

"The vessel stopped without further incident," JIATF-S said.

During follow-on operations, Coast Guard crews discovered what officials described as a "bale field" along the vessel's prior track and recovered the suspected marijuana, valued at more than $2.4 million.
"This mission required vigilance, professionalism, and seamless coordination from detection and pursuit to evidence recovery and search-and-rescue support," JIATF-S said.
WHITE HOUSE HIGHLIGHTS 'STEEPEST' EVER DECLINE IN US CASUALTIES FROM CARTELS AMID BOAT STRIKES
Coast Guard crews discovered what officials described as a "bale field" along the vessel's prior route before recovering 47 bales of suspected marijuana. (Joint Interagency Task Force South)

JIATF-S did not specify where the incident took place, but thanked the Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba and Joint Rescue Coordination Center Haiti for their "timely support, search assistance, and coordination throughout the operation."
The drug seizure comes amid the Trump administration's ongoing campaign targeting narcotics trafficking networks in the Western Hemisphere.
U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) touted the operation, saying the "bust is another demonstration of the United States' resolve to stop the flow of dangerous drugs into the homeland."

This week, SOUTHCOM said it conducted two operations in which U.S. forces intercepted and sank vessels in the Eastern Pacific that the military said were tied to Los Choneros, which it described as a violent narco-terrorist organization.
US KILLS TWO 'NARCO-TERRORISTS' IN STRIKE 2 MONTHS SINCE LAST ANNOUNCED ANTI-'NARCO-TRAFFICKING' ATTACK

More than $2.4 million worth of suspected marijuana was recovered during a Coast Guard operation involving a suspicious go-fast vessel, according to military officials. (Joint Interagency Task Force South)

The U.S. military has also been involved in a monthslong campaign launched by the Trump administration aimed at dismantling cartel-linked trafficking networks, including dozens of strikes in the Eastern Pacific and Caribbean targeting vessels it says are connected to "narco-terrorists."

The latest seizure follows another major Coast Guard drug bust off the coast of Puerto Rico last month.
The Coast Guard intercepted a suspected smuggling boat nearly 50 miles off the coast of the U.S. territory and discovered more than 7,000 pounds of cocaine worth about $54.5 million.

One of Karen Read’s former defense attorneys praised Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer for his work as jurors neared the end of a sixth day of deliberations — after twice telling the judge they could not reach a unanimous verdict.

"It immediately brings back the stress and the pressure that comes from having somebody's life in your hands and the very worst part of a trial, which is when the jury's out," said David Yannetti, who was key to Read's defense team through both of her Massachusetts murder trials. title: Lindsay Clancy jury wraps day 6 with bombshell one-juror standoff, deliberations to resume Friday
summary: Lindsay Clancy’s jury ended its sixth day without a verdict after a dispute involving a holdout juror, with deliberations set to resume Friday.
story: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports as jury deliberations enter a sixth day in the Lindsay Clancy trial and questions emerge over whether the panel can reach a unanimous verdict. Llenas details defense attorney Kevin Reddington’s claim that one juror is refusing to follow the law on reasonable doubt and the latest developments from the courtroom on ‘The Story.’
The jury deciding Lindsay Clancy’s fate ended a dramatic sixth day of deliberations Thursday without a verdict amid a dispute involving a holdout juror, with deliberations set to resume Friday.

The panel of nine women and three men has twice reported being deadlocked. Jurors are expected to return Friday, when Judge William Sullivan is also set to address a dispute involving one member of the panel.

Earlier Thursday, defense attorney Kevin Reddington unsuccessfully sought to remove a juror after the foreperson reported that the person was refusing to follow the court’s instructions on reasonable doubt.
Reddington warned that the case could end without a verdict because of a juror who had "spurned the instructions" of the court.
LINDSAY CLANCY JURY RECAP: DAY 5 ENDS WITH NO VERDICT AFTER RARE INSTRUCTION

Lindsay Clancy and Kevin Reddington listen to Judge Sullivan ask the jury to continue deliberations during Clancy's murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

Prosecutors objected to removing anyone, arguing there was no way to determine who was right or wrong without improperly examining the jury’s private deliberations. They said Sullivan had acted appropriately by questioning the jurors about whether they could follow the law and again instructing them on reasonable doubt.
WHAT IS A TUEY-RODRIGUEZ CHARGE? JUDGE GIVES INSTRUCTION TO DEADLOCKED LINDSAY CLANCY JURY
Sullivan declined, calling the removal of a deliberating juror "a sensitive undertaking" and saying the court could not take sides in the jury’s deliberations.
After court, Reddington revealed that a later jury note appeared to show an 11-to-1 divide.
SOCIAL MEDIA IS LINDSAY CLANCY WILD CARD THAT COULD TILT POTENTIAL RETRIAL TO THE DEFENSE, RETIRED JUDGE SAYS

Kevin J. Reddington addresses the media outside of Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday, September 3, 2026. His client, Lindsay Clancy, is on trial for the murder of her three children in 2023. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
"When a note that the judge already has says that there are 11 jurors that have made a decision and one juror will not apply reasonable [doubt]... ," Reddington said.
The note does not reveal which verdict the 11 jurors favor or how the remaining juror is leaning.
HARVEY WEINSTEIN RAPE TRIAL ENDS IN MISTRIAL AFTER JURY DEADLOCKED
The empty Plymouth Superior Court jury box during the Lindsay Clancy murder trial in Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool The Patriot Ledger via AP)
Reddington said Sullivan plans to hold an inquiry at 9 a.m. Friday. If jurors again say they cannot reach a unanimous decision, the case could end in a mistrial.
The defense attorney said he expects the arguments over the jury issue to take place in open court rather than at sidebar.
LINDSAY CLANCY’S FUTURE COULD REST WITH ‘PROSECUTION DOCTORS’ AS CASE ECHOES INFAMOUS MAINE KILLINGS: EXPERT
Asked whether a retrial could favor prosecutors, Reddington issued a blunt response.
"Bring it," he said, adding that his witnesses and evidence are ready.
"I got witnesses lined up. We’re all set. Dr. Resnick is ready. I’m ready. We’ve got all our evidence. Witnesses are available, so let’s go," Reddington said.

Lindsay Clancy's lawyer, Kevin J. Reddington, arrives at Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Tuesday, September 1, 2026. Clancy's murder trial enters its fourth day of jury deliberation today. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)

Reddington said prosecutors might seek to put off another trial "for six months or a year," but indicated he would be ready to move quickly. He deferred to Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz when questioned about the possibility of a plea agreement.
"Let’s see what Mr. Cruz wants to do, and then we’ll talk about our options," Reddington said.

Clancy, 36, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, Cora, Dawson and Callan, who were all under the age of 6 when they were found strangled in the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.
LINDSAY CLANCY VERDICT: RETIRED JUDGE EXPLAINS WHAT HAPPENS IF INSANITY DEFENSE PREVAILS
Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)
She does not dispute killing them. Jurors must instead decide whether she was criminally responsible at the time.

Prosecutors argue Clancy understood what she was doing and should be held responsible for the children’s deaths. Her attorneys contend she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and could not appreciate the wrongfulness of her actions or conform her conduct to the law.

title: WATCH: Bystanders, police lift Volkswagen off woman pinned underneath after dramatic e-bike crash
summary: Body camera video captured strangers and officers lifting a Volkswagen Beetle off a trapped e-bike rider after a crash on a Prospect Park road.
story: A police bodycam captured officers and bystanders rushing to lift a Volkswagen Beetle and free a 44-year-old woman who became pinned beneath the car after an e-bike crash in Prospect Park, Pennsylvania. (Credit: WTXF)

A group of strangers and police officers rushed to lift a Volkswagen Beetle off an injured e-bike rider after she became trapped beneath the car during a crash on a busy Pennsylvania road, dramatic body camera video shows.

Local authorities said the 44-year-old woman suffered several broken bones in Monday morning's crash in Prospect Park but survived after roughly six bystanders joined officers to lift the vehicle and pull her to safety, FOX 29 reported.

Prospect Park Police Chief Dave Madonna said the woman was riding an e-bike more than 20 mph, according to his estimate, without a helmet when she collided with the Volkswagen at an intersection along Route 420.

"She was driving way too fast for that time of day, for the road she was traveling on," Madonna said, adding that he believed she had been trying to overtake vehicles while traveling to an appointment.
RESCUERS FREE CLIMBER TRAPPED BENEATH 16,000-POUND BOULDER ON OREGON'S MOUNT HOOD IN COMPLEX OPERATION
Bystanders and police officers work together to lift a Volkswagen Beetle off an e-bike rider who became trapped beneath the vehicle after a crash in Prospect Park, Pa. (WTXF)
Surveillance and police body camera video shows bystanders rushing to the crash to help.
About six people then work together to lift the car high enough to free the woman trapped underneath.
"Got a yell to help, ran over. We lifted the Volkswagen Beetle up, pulled the girl out and pushed her to the ground so she wouldn't move, that's all," FedEx driver Carl Wise told the station.
GOOD SAMARITAN IN SPIDER-MAN COSTUME HELPS MAN IN WHEELCHAIR CROSS BUSY INTERSECTION IN VIRAL MOMENT
Police body camera video shows bystanders rushing to help lift a car off a 44-year-old e-bike rider following a crash along Route 420 in Pennsylvania. (WTXF)
"I'm no hero. I'm just a guy doing a job, that's all," he added.
Local business owner Chrissy Vollmer, who also responded, described what she saw.
"All I saw were the lady's legs underneath the car, and she was just yelling, ‘Get this car off of me,’" Vollmer said.
Madonna called the bystanders who helped rescue the woman "heroes" and later visited them to offer his thanks.
ICE OFFICER HAILED AS HERO AFTER SAVING DRIVER INJURED IN MISSOURI CRASH
About six bystanders joined police officers to lift a Volkswagen Beetle and free a woman trapped underneath, according to local authorities. (WTXF)
He also raised concerns about what he described as an increase in e-bike crashes.
"How many more tragedies do we have to see before some type of action is taken?" Madonna said.
The woman was taken to Lankenau Hospital and underwent surgery for a broken collarbone and other injuries, FOX 29 reported.

title: Officials identify victims killed, officers injured in Minneapolis apartment shooting
summary: Minnesota officials identified the two civilians killed and the Minneapolis police officers injured during Wednesday’s deadly apartment shooting.
story: Fox News' Chanley Painter has the latest on the response to the crime on 'Fox News @ Night.'
Minnesota officials released the identities of the victims involved in Wednesday’s Minneapolis apartment shooting that left two civilians dead and two police officers injured by gunfire.

The two civilians were Dale Henry Spry, 63, and Muse A. Afrah, 61, according to the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA). Officials previously said one victim died at the apartment complex and the other died at a hospital.

Both victims are believed to have been residents of the apartment complex where Carlton Neal Johnson II, 35, opened fire before he was fatally struck in an exchange of gunfire with police. A preliminary autopsy indicated Johnson died after sustaining multiple gunshot wounds, and his death was ruled a homicide, officials said.

The two Minneapolis Police Department (MPD) officers injured in the shooting were identified as Joseph Michnowski, a five-year veteran, and Yahye Ahmed, a nearly two-year veteran, according to the BCA.
3 DEAD, INCLUDING SUSPECTED GUNMAN, AND 3 OFFICERS INJURED IN MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING
The suspected gunman in the shooting in downtown Minneapolis reportedly was facing eviction from an apartment building. (Ellen Schmidt/AP)
Ahmed was released from a hospital Thursday, while Michnowski remained hospitalized Thursday afternoon, interim Police Chief Bill Peterson said during a briefing.
Garrett Parten, an MPD public information officer, said one of the injured officers sustained an apparent non-life-threatening gunshot wound to the leg, while the other underwent surgery.
Another officer involved in the incident was also evaluated for an apparent non-life-threatening injury, Parten said.
MINNEAPOLIS APARTMENT SHOOTING SUSPECT WAS FACING EVICTION: REPORT
Officers investigating the aftermath of a shooting in Minneapolis Wednesday. (Ellen Schmidt/AP Photo)

Peterson identified the third officer as Ernest Boateng but clarified that his injuries were not directly related to the gunfire. Boateng was cut by glass while breaking a window of a locked police vehicle whose sirens were going off, Peterson said.
Boateng was evaluated and released Wednesday.
The BCA said at least one officer discharged his gun during the incident, identifying the officer as Liban Mohamed Ibrahim, a two-year MPD veteran.
"Investigators are continuing to determine whether any other officers fired their weapons," BCA said.
Law enforcement responds to a shooting in Minneapolis Wednesday. (Ellen Schmidt/AP Photo)

Wednesday’s shooting began during a domestic child custody exchange involving a woman who previously had a relationship with Johnson, according to Drew Evans, superintendent of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension.

Johnson reportedly shot the woman outside the building before going inside the apartment, where he shot another facility worker. He then went to the ninth floor, where he shot two residents who later died.
He was also facing eviction from the apartment building, according to court records obtained by Fox9 Minneapolis.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Officials have not determined whether Johnson specifically targeted the victims.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Trump names Adam Telle acting secretary of the Army following Dan Driscoll's resignation
summary: Adam Telle steps in as acting Army secretary after Dan Driscoll's resignation amid reported clashes with Pete Hegseth over Army readiness efforts.
story: Fox News chief national security correspondent Jennifer Griffin discusses Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitting his resignation to President Donald Trump, the reported tensions within Pentagon leadership and the latest developments in the escalating U.S.-Iran conflict, including what the shake-up could mean for America's military strategy and national security on 'America Reports.'
President Donald Trump on Thursday announced he was appointing Adam Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for Civil Works, as acting secretary of the Army.
"I am pleased to announce that Adam Telle, the current Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, will become Acting Secretary of the Army, effective immediately," Trump posted on Truth Social.
"He is a Great Patriot, who is respected by all."
He made the announcement after Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to the president earlier this week.
ARMY SECRETARY DAN DRISCOLL SUBMITS RESIGNATION TO TRUMP
President Donald Trump appointed Adam Telle as acting secretary of the Army after the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll. (Kent Nishimura/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Telle, who was nominated by Trump and confirmed by the Senate in 2025, oversees the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Civil Works program, where his responsibilities include flood and storm protection, commercial waterways and Clean Water Act permitting.

Previously, Telle served as chief of staff to Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., and was Trump's chief liaison to the Senate during the president's first administration, when he led the White House Office of Legislative Affairs' Senate team.

Before that, Telle served on the Senate Appropriations Committee subcommittee responsible for overseeing the Department of Homeland Security's budget. He also spent 10 years in the office of former Sen. Thad Cochran, R-Miss., where he served as deputy chief of staff, legislative director and the senator's top national security staffer.
TRUMP’S ARMY SECRETARY HUNT TAKES SHAPE AS INSIDERS FLOAT POTENTIAL PICKS

U.S. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll, War Secretary Pete Hegseth and President Donald Trump attend a dignified transfer at Dover Air Force Base for military casualties of the war with Iran July 22, 2026, in Dover, Del. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
Telle is viewed as having strong relationships with senators on Capitol Hill, which could prove important as the administration works to confirm Army nominees stalled in the Senate.
The appointment fills a key leadership vacancy atop the nation's largest military branch.

Driscoll's exit came after he reportedly butted heads with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth over the Army's transformation and readiness, including Driscoll's belief that Hegseth had hindered those efforts, Fox News Digital previously reported.
US ARMY OFFERING DEFENSE FIRMS 'CONCIERGE ACCESS' TO TEST WEAPONS AT MILITARY RANGES
President Donald Trump announced that Adam Telle would become acting secretary of the Army "effective immediately," calling him a "Great Patriot." (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)
The outgoing Army secretary said Wednesday would be his "last full day" in the position, adding that serving under Trump and Hegseth had been "the honor of a lifetime."

"I had the privilege of working with them to modernize and accelerate how the Army mans, trains, and equips the most lethal fighting force on the face of the earth," Driscoll said in a statement posted on X.
"We could not have made the progress we did without the support of Secretary Hegseth," he continued. "I am forever grateful to President Trump for the opportunity to once again serve my country."

title: EXCLUSIVE: FBI extraditions soar as Patel ramps up foreign outreach, vows 'no sanctuary'
summary: FBI Director Kash Patel says FBI extraditions of international fugitives to the United States are up 65%, with 157 executed amid a sweeping manhunt push.
story: Arizona murder suspect Varun Batchigari faces extradition from Germany after his arrest in the killing of girlfriend Julissa Salazar. Former DOJ prosecutor Jim Trusty analyzes the international legal hurdles in bringing the suspect back to face charges, while discussing Vice President JD Vance's warning about migrant welfare fraud.
FIRST ON FOX: FBI Director Kash Patel has dramatically expanded direct outreach to foreign partners in an effort to bring international fugitives back to the United States.

FBI data exclusively obtained by Fox News Digital shows Patel made 100 calls to international partners in his first 18 months, compared with nine by his predecessor during the final 18 months of the Biden administration.

Compared to the last 18 months of the Biden administration, extraditions were up 65%, and FTOCs (foreign transfer of custody), in which a fugitive or suspect is apprehended overseas and transferred into U.S. custody, are up 54%, the FBI said.
In that time, the FBI has executed 157 extraditions and 86 FTOCs.
FBI BRINGS BACK FUGITIVE ACCUSED IN $3.7B MEDICARE FRAUD SCHEME AFTER CAPTURE IN TURKEY

FBI Director Kash Patel touted the agency's facilitation of foreign transfers of custody and the uptick in extraditions of high-profile targets seeking to evade U.S. justice abroad. (Win McNamee/Getty Images/File)
"When I became FBI director, I made clear that we would relentlessly manhunt high‑value targets from overseas, and we’ve delivered," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital.

"It’s a direct result of President [Donald] Trump’s relationships with foreign governments, which allow us to work in spaces where we were never permitted to before and Attorney General Todd Blanche’s leadership giving us the legal tools we need to return these subjects back to America to face charges.
"These targets are literally the worst of the worst, and we will give them no sanctuary."
MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE ON WEDDING NIGHT BROUGHT BACK TO US AFTER YEARS ON THE RUN IN MEXICO
Alexis Flores was previously a top 10 FBI fugitive, according to officials. He was arrested Wednesday in Honduras in the 2000 murder of a young girl in Philadelphia. (FBI and Google Maps)

On Monday, a Honduran citizen on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted Fugitives list was extradited to Philadelphia after 25 years on the run for the alleged rape and murder of a 5-year-old girl, Fox News exclusively reported.

Alexis Flores was arrested in February, and Honduran authorities agreed to extradite him to the U.S. The FBI said Flores had been removed from the fugitives list in March 2025 due to the prior Honduran government’s refusal to extradite him for his offenses, citing local laws limiting extradition.
EXCLUSIVE: ALLEGED $32M COVID-19 FRAUD FUGITIVE CAPTURED IN JAMAICA AND RETURNED TO US, FBI SAYS
FBI agents escort Zobaidul Amin after his transfer from Malaysia to the United States to face charges in an alleged international sextortion and child exploitation scheme. (Department of Justice)
Since June, the FBI has conducted more than 70 extraditions, Patel said at the time of Flores' extradition to the U.S.
In March, Zobaidul Amin, a Bangladeshi national, was extradited from Malaysia to the U.S. to face charges related to one of the most prolific online child exploitation schemes.

Prosecutors allege Amin posed as a teenager on Instagram and Snapchat and coerced hundreds of minor victims — some as young as 11 — into producing sexually explicit images and videos. Authorities said he then threatened to share those images with friends, family and classmates unless the victims sent more.

Another recent example is the case of Abdullah Anwar, 28, a Texas resident who was brought back from Qatar to face fraud charges. Anwar fled the U.S. for Pakistan but was arrested in Qatar before authorities there agreed to extradite him to Texas.
FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

The FBI has prioritized the extradition of suspects and fugitives abroad. From 2022 to 2025, former FBI Director Christopher Wray made 20 calls to foreign partners, including nine in his last 18 months during the Biden administration, the agency said.
Patel has made 100 calls in his first 18 months, a 400% increase over those made during Wray's four years and a 1,011% call increase over Wray's final 18 months with the Biden administration.
FBI agents stand on the tarmac as a plane arrives carrying Zobaidul Amin after his extradition from Malaysia to face federal charges in Alaska. (Department of Justice)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Typically, the FBI works with foreign authorities and governments to track and arrest suspects hiding in other countries. Once someone is arrested, the Justice Department will formally request that person be handed over to U.S. custody using existing international treaties.
Once the foreign government approves the handover, FBI agents travel abroad, take physical custody of the fugitive and fly them back to the U.S. for trial.

title: Anti-migrant AfD seeks to break Germany’s political ‘firewall’ in historic state election
summary: Young voters are fueling Germany's AfD surge in Saxony-Anhalt, where lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund has amassed over 700,000 TikTok followers.
story: Nile Gardiner weighs in after European voters appeared to reject far-left progressive policies, leading to significant conservative gains across the continent.

A political earthquake is brewing in Germany's east as working-class and young voters appear set to deliver an unprecedented victory for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in Sunday’s state elections in Saxony-Anhalt.

The AfD, which was famously backed by Elon Musk in last year’s national election, has been criticized for being pro-Russia and was accused of being a "right-wing extremist endeavor" by Germany’s domestic intelligence office, has the chance to become the first party outside the mainstream center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) or center-right Christian Democratic Union and their Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU), to win an outright majority in a German state parliament, or Landtag, since World War II.

"The reason Saxony-Anhalt matters," foreign policy expert and author Daniel Schatz, who holds a doctorate in political science from Berlin's Humboldt University, told Fox News Digital, "is that the AfD is no longer just knocking on the door of power. It may be close to kicking it open."
TENS OF THOUSANDS OF FAR-LEFT PROTESTERS CLASH WITH POLICE IN ANTI-CONSERVATIVE PARTY RIOTS

Ulrich Siegmund, a charismatic candidate with broad appeal in the state, has helped propel the AfD to 43% in state polls, far ahead of other parties. The AfD could possibly win with a majority in the state parliament and form a state government, which would be a first for the party. Saxony-Anhalt will hold elections on Sept. 6. (Getty Images)

Other minor parties have led governing coalitions in German states, but no party outside the SPD or the CDU and the CSU has ever held a single-party governing majority in Germany since the Federal Republic was re-established in 1949.

Janek Treiber, a political science researcher at Dresden University of Technology, told Fox News Digital that if the AfD does win outright in Saxony-Anhalt, their policy influence would be limited due to the German federal system, but warned "you must not underestimate the political symbol this would give. That a single party, and a right-wing party, could rule a German state… The symbol that these parties, that have been ruling Germany since 1949 or the East since 1990, they now lose control. They now lose power. I think this is a much more important symbol than just saying, OK, (the) AfD will change this or that in its local school system or university system."

Schatz described the AfD "a nationalist, anti-immigration party on the far right that has become a powerful vehicle for voter anger at Germany’s political establishment — especially in the former East Germany. It campaigns for much tighter immigration, a stronger emphasis on German national identity, rejection of much of the green agenda and a softer line toward Russia."

An outright win for the AfD, even in Germany’s sixth smallest state, would break through the political establishment’s so-called "Brandmauer," or "firewall." Simply put, other parties refuse to work with the AfD, which is currently the second-largest party in the Bundestag, officially the opposition party, after winning 20.8% of the vote in the February 2025 federal election.
'SEND THEM BACK' CHANTS ROCK EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AFTER LANDSLIDE VOTE TO SPEED UP DEPORTATIONS
The AfD's lead candidate, Ulrich Siegmund, campaigns during the 2026 state election in Saxony-Anhalt. (Sebastian Willnow/picture alliance via Getty Images)

In an interview on German broadcaster ZDF, the AfD’s national co-chair, Alice Weidel, advocated for closing Germany’s borders and exiting Europe’s Schengen treaty, saying, "Illegal migration, unchecked open borders, anyone can get in. Our internal security is suffering. People are honestly fed up with this situation."

Weidel added, "All Syrian refugees must have their protected status revoked because the reason for their flight no longer exists. These people must return to their homeland. If they don't leave voluntarily, then they must be deported by force." Adding that many of the 1.3 million Syrians in Germany are being naturalized, "we must stop naturalizing these people who should actually be leaving our country. We have Islamization."
GERMAN OFFICIALS WANT TO KNOW WHY BERLIN ATTACK SUSPECT WAS FREE DESPITE ALLEGED ISIS SUPPORT

Regional elections in the eastern federal state of Saxony-Anhalt will take place on Sept. 6, 2026, and two weeks later, the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and the capital Berlin itself will also elect their state assemblies on Sept.20, 2026. (Ronny Hartmann/AFP via Getty Images)

In May 2025, Germany's Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) classified the AfD as a "confirmed right-wing extremist" group, citing "anti-migrant positions and an ancestry-based definition of German identity." This past February, according to Deutsche Welle, that classification was put on hold by a German court after "Judges found that while there was evidence of potentially unconstitutional statements and policies within the AfD… it said that there was not sufficient evidence to characterize the party as a whole as extremist."

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz recently told state broadcaster ARD, "I cannot imagine international investors attending a ground-breaking ceremony with an AfD Minister-President to set up new plants and establish new businesses in Saxony-Anhalt… However, that is a decision for ​the voters in Saxony-Anhalt to make. The state will suffer ⁠considerable damage if things turn out as we now fear they ​might."
This has done little to damage the popularity of the AfD’s lead candidate in Saxony-Anhalt, Ulrich Siegmund. In a state of just over 2 million people, he has a TikTok following of over 700,000.

A Center for Strategic & International Studies (CSIS) report said Siegmund’s "polished appearance and professional tone lend respectability, and radical demands blend with footage of a community-oriented politician responding to audience questions… The AfD’s physical presence in the streets and omnipresence in the media helps to push the common populist ‘us versus them’ narrative: The AfD is here for you, the other parties are not."
NEW GERMANY SEX-CRIME FIGURES REIGNITE MIGRATION FIGHT AS EXPLOITATION PROBE EXPANDS
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz sparked backlash while remarking about the country's migration policies. (Thomas Traasdahl/Ritzau Scanpix via AP)

According to the independent, non-partisan German website Wahlrecht.de, which tracks federal and state election polling, ahead of Sunday’s vote in Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD holds a 41%-23% lead over the CDU, followed by three leftist parties. A party or a coalition needs at least half of the seats to control parliament and name a state minister-president, essentially a governor. So how can a party with only 43% win an election outright? That comes down to Germany’s unique election system.

"German voters cast two ballots," Schatz says, "One for a local candidate — like voting for your congressman — and one for a party. That second vote, the party vote, is the one that counts. It decides how many seats each party gets in parliament." But there is a caveat: "Any party that falls below 5% gets nothing — zero seats — and those votes are effectively thrown out. Right now, several smaller parties are hovering right at that line. If they miss it, 42% or 43% of the vote can translate into more than half the seats. So Saxony-Anhalt could wake up to an AfD majority government even though a clear majority of voters chose someone else. That would be a first in postwar Germany."

The CSIS report said voters are drawn to the AfD "because, or despite of, its extremist ideology. 60.5% of AfD voters hold a right-wing extremist worldview… At the same time, more than two in five AfD voters think that the party does not sufficiently distance itself from right-wing extremist positions." The report also found that AfD’s "strongest recent gains have been among voters 18 to 25 years old, where the party tripled its results compared to the 2021 national election."

Treiber said economics is pushing younger voters to the AfD, due to rising expenses and unemployment. He also said younger voters are "kind of polarized because the other part of the youth in Germany is voting for the left party (Die Linke)."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Saxony-Anhalt may just be the beginning for the anti-establishment parties. Voters in neighboring Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where former Chancellor Angela Merkel grew up and began her political career, go to the polls in two weeks. Polling data from Wahlrecht.de shows the AfD leading the ruling SPD 35%-32% there.

Conversely, in Berlin, where voters in the capital also go to the polls in two weeks, the average of recent polling has the far-left Die Linke in a dead heat with the CDU at 20%, followed by the AfD at 18%, with the Greens and the SPD each around 15%. While the majority of the AfD’s support does come from the former East Germany, the party is represented in 14 of Germany’s 16 state legislatures and holds 15 of Germany’s 96 seats in the European Parliament.

Tyler Speicher is an American journalist living in Slovenia after spending 25 years covering stories ranging from the Little League World Series to hurricanes, 9/11 and its aftermath for New York City news outlets, including 20 years on the Fox News Channel assignment desk.

title: Fighter jet crashes at air show, killing 2 pilots with thousands of spectators watching
summary: Video captured a Phantom F-4 jet crashing into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver at Tanagra Air Force Base as thousands witnessed it.
story: A Greek air force fighter jet crashed and burst into flames during an air show with thousands of spectators. (Credit: @sovva1_1 via Storyful and REUTERS).
A day at an air show turned fatal Saturday when a Greek air force jet crashed north of Athens as thousands of spectators watched.
Both pilots were killed in the crash at Tanagra Air Force Base, but no civilians were hurt.
The twin-seat Phantom F-4 jet flew into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver just meters above the ground.
EIGHT BELIEVED DEAD AFTER B-52 CRASHES SHORTLY AFTER TAKEOFF FROM EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE

Spectators watch as smoke rises after a Hellenic Air Force F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed during the Athens Flying Week airshow at Tanagra Air Force Base, north of Athens, Greece, Saturday. (AP Photo/Kallista Allaway)

"The sense of grief is widespread, and our thoughts are with the families of the two pilots we lost," Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said. "It is a reminder of the daily danger faced by Greece’s aviators, who remain on constant standby to protect Greece's skies."
The jet burst into flames on impact, sending up a large plume of black smoke, prompting 11 water-dropping planes and helicopters to assist 85 firefighters in extinguishing the blaze.
11 SKYDIVERS, ONE PILOT KILLED IN MISSOURI PLANE CRASH NEAR AIRPORT
Video of the crash showed a second ball of fire nearby as the plane broke apart.
The bodies of the pilots were eventually recovered.
Smoke rises after a Hellenic Air Force F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed during the Athens Flying Week airshow at Tanagra Air Force Base, north of Athens, Greece, Saturday. (AP Photo/undefined)
"We were all stunned. It hadn't been airborne for more than three minutes," an eyewitness told ERT, Greece’s state-owned broadcaster.
The crash happened during the country’s annual Athens Flying Week.
The organizers canceled the rest of the events after the incident, and the area was evacuated.
Two pilots were killed in the crash. (Reuters)

"It is with deep sadness that I learned of the death of the two officers of the Hellenic Air Force, who lost their lives in the tragic accident that occurred during the air show at Tanagra Air Base," Cyprus' Defense Minister Vasilis Palmas said, adding he had called Nikos Dendias, Greece’s Minister of National Defense.
AIR FORCE IDENTIFIES 8 CREW MEMBERS KILLED IN B-52 STRATOFORTRESS CRASH AT EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE
The air force has declared three days of mourning in the country.

title: United Nations votes 164-1 for Equal Earth map after US brands it 'radical ideological project'
summary: The United Nations adopted the Equal Earth map showing Africa's true size, but the United States was the sole nation to vote against the resolution.
story: Yaryna Ferencevych, the deputy U.S. representative to the United Nations, voted against changing the official map of the world to reflect Africa's true size.
The United Nations on Friday was one vote shy of unanimously adopting a new map of the world that shows Africa's true size, making the continent appear far larger than it does on traditional maps.

The United States was the only one of 165 member nations to vote against the U.N. General Assembly resolution to accept the Equal Earth map projection, which depicts countries and continents in their true relative sizes, according to the map creator's website.
Six nations abstained, including Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine.

Yaryna Ferencevych, the deputy U.S. representative to the U.N. Economic and Social Council, said the resolution was presented as "an anodyne effort to update cartographic proportions" but was, in her view, part of a "much larger and more radical ideological project."

Yaryna Ferencevych, the deputy U.S. representative to the United Nations Economic and Social Council, speaks against adopting the Equal Earth world map during the 114th plenary meeting of the 80th session of the U.N. General Assembly Sept. 4, 2026. (United Nations)
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION REJECTS UN MIGRATION DECLARATION, SAYS 'MASS MIGRATION WAS NEVER SAFE'

"Instead of focusing on genuine problems of international peace, prosperity or good relations, this body is debating map projects from the 16th century and their role in promoting reparations and cognitive justice," Ferencevych said Friday during the 114th Plenary meeting.
"Resolutions like this one and the ideological agenda they promote are barnacles on our work here and the reason this institution is losing its credibility."

Ferencevych was referring to the Mercator projection, created in 1569 to aid maritime navigation. To this day, it is seen as the traditional world map and is used in many school textbooks and atlases.
It enlarges land masses near the poles and reduces the apparent size of those near the equator, making Africa appear far smaller relative to Greenland and Europe than it is in reality.
The Equal Earth map that the United Nations favors. It depicts all continents at their true sizes relative to one another. (Courtesy: Tom Patterson)
AFRICAN AND CARIBBEAN LEADERS CALL FOR PAYMENTS, DEBT CANCELLATION, FORMAL APOLOGIES OVER SLAVERY

Togo Foreign Minister Robert Dussey, who introduced the resolution on behalf of the African Group, said adopting the new map would "promote projections that better preserve the true proportions of continents."

"A fair map does not change the geography of the world; it changes how we see the world," he said. "And when our perspective becomes more just, it paves the way for greater understanding, respect and peace among nations."
The measure does not require countries or companies to abandon the Mercator projection, but it establishes the U.N.'s official backing for equal-area maps as the preferred way to depict the world.
The world on Mercator projection between 85°3'4"S and 85°3'4"N. (Strebe)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Mercator projection largely fell out of favor among cartographers in the 20th century because of its distortions. However, it saw a resurgence after Google Maps adopted the Web Mercator projection in 2005, with virtually every major online mapping service following suit.

Web Mercator became the standard for online maps because it allowed for smooth panning and zooming across the globe, making it well suited for interactive digital maps, according to a 2014 Cartographica study.
The United States Mission to the United Nations and the ECOSOC did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

title: Trump negotiators Witkoff, Kushner meet with Putin in Moscow as US pushes for end to Russia-Ukraine war
summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Vladimir Putin in Moscow for peace talks before heading to Kyiv, and President Donald Trump says there may be a good chance for a deal.
story: Russian President Vladimir Putin greets U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the Kremlin on Saturday for talks on ending Russia's war with Ukraine. (The Associated Press)

U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump's son-in-law and advisor, Jared Kushner, met with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin in Moscow on Saturday, as part of a weekend journey that will take them to Kyiv on Sunday in an effort to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Witkoff and Kushner met with Putin for more than three hours behind closed doors, The Associated Press reported, and concluded without any breakthroughs.
The AP said Putin’s foreign policy advisor, Yuri Ushakov, called the talks constructive, frank and useful.

"Today, Special Envoy Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with President Vladimir Putin of Russia to advance President Trump's agenda of peace in the Russia-Ukraine War. They were joined by officials from the National Security Council, State Department, and Treasury Department to discuss proposals to bring peace to this conflict," a White House official said after Saturday's talks. "The American delegation also thanked President Putin for releasing former United States Marine Robert Gilman from Russian custody out of respect for President Trump.
"The two sides discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks, and look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow in Ukraine."
TRUMP ANNOUNCES SURPRISE THREE-DAY CEASEFIRE IN RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

President Vladimir Putin, right, greets U.S. envoys Jared Kushner, left, and Steve Witkoff, center, prior to talks at the Senate Palace of the Kremlin in Moscow, on Saturday. (Mikhail Metzel/Sputnik/Kremlin Pool Photo via AP)
On Friday, Trump addressed Saturday's anticipated visit with reporters.

"We have an idea for peace. I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators," he said. "They've done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we'll do it."
Kushner and Witkoff visited Russia first on Saturday, and were greeted by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev shortly after landing in Moscow.
Kushner and Witkoff will be Kyiv on Sunday to meet with Ukrainian President Volodomyr Zelenskyy.
In a post on X, Zelenskyy said Ukraine will work to keep Russian airspace safe during the Americans’ visit.
CIA DIRECTOR JOHN RATCLIFFE MET WITH RUSSIAN INTELLIGENCE OFFICIALS IN VISIT TO MOSCOW, KREMLIN SAYS

U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff, right, Jared Kushner, center, and Presidential Envoy Kirill Dmitriev stand prior to talks at the Senate Palace of the Kremlin in Moscow, on Saturday. (Gavriil Grigorov/Sputnik/Kremlin Pool Photo via AP)

"Just as we did during previous diplomatic visits by the American side, we will ensure the normal functioning of Russian airspace so that the negotiators can arrive safely. We are looking out for them, not for Russia. There will be no air strikes from our side, and Russia must do the same, ensuring there are no air strikes from its side for the time needed to hold these talks and handle the logistical matters related to this American visit," Zelenskyy wrote.

"Our goal is to make the visit and the talks with the U.S. side as constructive and substantive as possible. We need to look for real options for how to move this war toward an end. We will see what proposals Steve and Jared bring and what they are told in Moscow in response."
ZELENSKYY CONGRATULATES TRUMP ON TURNING 80 IN BIRTHDAY CALL, VOWS MORE UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AT G7 ON TUESDAY
Zelenskyy’s message Friday came the same day a Russian drone strike targeted the Security Service of Ukraine’s headquarters in Ukraine. (@ZelenskyyUa via X)
Zelenskyy, in a subsequent Saturday morning post on X, said he had already communicated with Witkoff and Kushner ahead of their planned Sunday meeting.

"I have just spoken with the U.S. President’s envoys. They have already begun working with the Russian side today. From the moment of this conversation, we are ready to observe a ceasefire in airstrikes against the cities involved in the negotiation process. From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow, and we expect the Russians to do the same regarding Kyiv," Zelenskyy wrote.

"Today, I also received reports from Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Mykhailo Drapatyi on the situation at the front, the dynamics of threats in Ukraine’s airspace, our steps, and active defensive operations. I am grateful to every one of our warriors for effectively defending Ukraine’s positions," Zelenskyy's post continued.

"On the diplomatic track, our actions must be, and will be, just as strong and effective – one hundred percent. The plan for tomorrow’s diplomatic engagements in Kyiv, involving the U.S. team, has been approved. We are waiting for Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and are ready for a substantive conversation. Thank you to everyone who stands with Ukraine!"
PUTIN UNLEASHES NEW FURY ON UKRAINE AS REPORT EXPOSES FEAR HANGING OVER WAR’S END

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, right, greets U.S. special representatives Jared Kushner, center, and Steve Witkoff upon their arrival Saturday at Vnukovo International Airport in Moscow, Russia. (Reuters)
Zelenskyy’s message Friday came the same day a Russian drone strike targeted the Security Service of Ukraine’s headquarters in Ukraine, Zelenskyy wrote in a public message on the app Telegram.
Zelenskyy alleged the strike directly targeted the head of the Security Service's office.
He also wrote that he was directing the head, Oleksandr Poklad, to prepare a retaliatory strike.

"I gave Poklad the task of adequately, noticeably and, if possible, mirroring the Russians' response to this attack, when everything is prepared. Our military will support this response. Glory to Ukraine!" Zelenskyy wrote.
At least nine people were injured in the explosion, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko also wrote on Telegram.
RUSSIA’S STRIKES NEAR MOLDOVA RAISE ALARM OVER PUTIN’S PLANS FOR EUROPE’S EASTERN FLANK

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, center, walks with U.S. special representatives Jared Kushner, left, and Steve Witkoff upon their arrival Saturday at Vnukovo International Airport in Moscow, Russia. (Reuters)
The visit also comes just one day after German officials formally accused Russia of attempting an explosive drone attack on a major airport in Germany.
